### About the event

Last day of Devcon. Before you head to the closing party, spend one session on the thing that decides whether what you shipped this week survives contact with mainnet.

Ship Safe is QuillAudits' security session for Devcon Mumbai: real exploit teardowns, a practical audit-readiness clinic, and a panel on what actually broke in 2026 and why. Short talks, hard questions, then drinks.

### What to expect

Exploit teardowns: we walk through the biggest 2026 incidents line by line. Where the bug was, why the audit missed it, what the fix looked like.

Audit readiness: how to prepare a codebase so an audit finds real issues instead of formatting nits. Scoping, invariants, test coverage, what to freeze before review.

AI vs AI: how attackers are using AI to find bugs faster, and what AI-assisted auditing and formal verification change for teams shipping on tight timelines.

Panel: founders, auditors and researchers on the security debt building up across L2s, RWA and stablecoin rails, and what they would do differently.

Networking and drinks from 6:45 PM.

Who should come

Founders, CTOs and protocol engineers shipping on Ethereum and L2s. Security researchers and auditors. RWA, stablecoin and DeFi teams. Anyone who wants an honest look at how things break.

### About QuillAudits

8+ years securing Web3. 1,500+ audits, 1M+ lines reviewed, trusted by teams including StarkWare, Taiko, ZetaChain and Metis. Full lifecycle security: AI and human audits, OpSec, multisig review and monitoring.

Venue in BKC, Mumbai, shared with confirmed attendees. Seats are limited and every registration is reviewed.

### Solana Across Campuses - Smt. Indira Gandhi College of engineering

Location: Smt. Indira Gandhi College of engineering, Navi Mumbai

Date: 15 Sep

Powered by: College.xyz (https://College.xyz) × Solana Foundation

### About the Event

Ever heard of cryptocurrency or blockchain but never really understood what they are?

Or maybe you've heard names like Bitcoin, Ethereum, or Solana but never had the chance to explore how they actually work?

Solana Across Campuses is a student-focused initiative bringing an introduction to blockchain technology and the Solana ecosystem directly to university campuses.

Our campus meetup is designed especially for beginners. You don't need to know anything about blockchain, cryptocurrency, programming, or Web3 to attend.

The goal is simple: learn, explore, and experience the technology yourself.

During the session, we'll break down what blockchain and cryptocurrency actually mean in simple terms, introduce you to Solana, show you how digital wallets work, and demonstrate some real applications built using this technology.

Whether you're a computer science student, designer, entrepreneur, finance enthusiast, or simply someone curious about new technology, you're welcome.

No prior experience. No technical background. Just curiosity.

### What Will You Learn?

What is Blockchain?

We'll start from the very beginning.

- What exactly is a blockchain?
- Why do people use it?
- How is it different from a normal database?
- Where is cryptocurrency used?
- What problems can this technology solve?

No complicated terminology - we'll keep it simple and practical.

What is Solana?

You'll get an introduction to Solana, a blockchain network designed for fast and low-cost digital transactions and applications.

We'll explore:

- What Solana is
- How it works at a basic level
- What people are building on it
- Why developers and startups are interested in it
- How students can start exploring the ecosystem

Create Your First Digital Wallet

Get a hands-on introduction to how a crypto wallet works.

You'll learn:

- What a digital wallet is
- How wallets store and manage digital assets
- How transactions work
- How to safely use a wallet

Depending on the event setup, participants may also have an opportunity to receive a small amount of SOL, the native cryptocurrency of the Solana network, to experience a transaction themselves.

Explore Real Applications

Blockchain isn't just about buying and selling cryptocurrency.

We'll demonstrate some of the applications being built using blockchain technology and show how the ecosystem is being used by developers, creators, entrepreneurs, and communities.

Opportunities for Students

Interested in technology or building something of your own?

We'll also introduce opportunities available in the ecosystem, including:

- Hackathons
- Developer programs
- Student communities
- Workshops
- Grants and startup opportunities
- Ways to start building on Solana

You don't have to be an expert or an experienced developer to get started.

### Agenda

Welcome & Check-in

Meet other students and get introduced to the event.

Blockchain & Crypto - Explained Simply

Understand the basics without assuming any prior knowledge.

Introduction to Solana

Learn what Solana is and why it has become an ecosystem for developers and applications.

Hands-on Wallet Setup

Learn how a digital wallet works and, where applicable, create your first wallet.

Live Demonstrations

Explore real applications and see how blockchain technology works in practice.

Building & Opportunities

Discover how students can participate in hackathons, communities, developer programs, and projects.

Interactive Activity / Challenge

Take part in a fun activity to test what you've learned and get a chance to win rewards.

Networking

Meet students interested in technology, startups, development, and emerging technologies.

Closing & Group Photo

Wrap up the session, connect with fellow participants, and stay connected with the campus community.

### Why Should You Attend?

Start From Zero

Never heard of blockchain before? That's completely fine. This event starts from the basics.

Learn a New Technology

Get a practical introduction to one of the technologies gaining attention across the global technology industry.

Try It Yourself

Don't just listen to explanations - experience how a digital wallet and blockchain transaction work.

Discover Opportunities

Learn about hackathons, developer programs, communities, and other opportunities for students.

Meet Like-Minded Students

Connect with students who are curious about technology, startups, development, and innovation.

Rewards & Swag

Participants may have opportunities to receive SOL, merchandise, or other event rewards, depending on availability.

### Who Can Attend?

Everyone.

You don't need to be:

A blockchain developer

A crypto trader

A computer science student

A Web3 expert

You can be:

A complete beginner

A developer

A designer

An entrepreneur

A finance or business student

A startup enthusiast

Someone curious about new technology

No prior knowledge of blockchain or cryptocurrency is required.

### One Question to Bring With You

"What exactly is this blockchain thing everyone keeps talking about?"

Come find out.

Join us for Solana Across Campuses and take your first step into the world of blockchain technology - no prior experience required.

### One Day. No Limits. Just Ship

Monad Blitz is storming into Mumbai for Blitz V4! This isn't your typical multi-day hackathon. It's a high-intensity, one-day IRL build sprint where you'll learn Monad, ship fast, and plug directly into one of the most exciting high-performance blockchain ecosystems today.

Since launching in 2025, Monad Blitz has energized builders from Shenzhen to San Francisco through 50+ Blitz Hacks. Now, the energy continues in Mumbai.

Get ready for an all-action day where you learn, build, vibe, and ship, all at ludicrous speed.

### THE VIBE

Mumbai Blitz isn't about fancy zones or over-engineered setups. It's about pure builder energy and a day dedicated to creating, collaborating, and shipping at speed.

Connect with Mumbai's Sharpest Builders

Meet some of the city's most talented developers. Share ideas, spark new ones, form teams instantly, and build alongside people who move as fast as you do.

Collaborate & Ship Wild Ideas

Come with an idea or discover one on the spot. Blitz is designed for momentum. Prototype fast, get real feedback, iterate quickly, and ship a consumer-ready dApp on Monad by evening.

Energise, Build, Repeat

Good food, good conversations, and a lot of code. Expect a full day of vibes, velocity, and execution.

### THE STAKES

$1,500 Prize Pool

- 1st Place: $500
- 2nd Place: $400
- 3rd Place: $300
- 4th Place: $200
- 5th Place: $100

Peer-Judged: Your fellow builders choose the winners. Zero Constraints: Build any consumer app on Monad. If it runs, it's fair game.

### THE FLOW

1. Learn: Morning workshops and hands-on mentoring to get you up to speed on Monad.
2. Build: 7 hours of high-speed execution. Form a team or go solo.
3. Ship: Demo your MVP to the crowd.
4. Win: Claim your share of the prize.

### WHY BLITZ?

Monad is built for speed, and Blitz is how we prove it.

We provide the environment, the mentors, and the brain fuel (yes, everything is purple). You bring the code.

Whether you're a seasoned EVM developer or just curious about high-performance blockchains, if you can ship, you belong here.

Event Date: 19 September

Applications close: 17 September

Capacity is limited. Apply early to secure your spot.

### WHO SHOULD APPLY?

Mumbai's best builders:

- Proven Builders: Show off your GitHub, portfolio, or past projects.
- Experimenters & Innovators: Bring that idea you've been itching to test.
- Fast Learners: You thrive in high-tempo environments.
- Community-Minded Devs: Ready to connect and join the Monad ecosystem.

Teams of up to 3 members allowed.

### About Monad

Monad is a high-performance, EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain built from the ground up for parallel execution.

With innovations in consensus and execution, Monad can scale to 10,000 TPS, enabling new classes of hyper-responsive, consumer-ready applications.

### About Monad Blitz

Monad Blitz is a global one-day hackathon series designed for speed, experimentation, and real output.

It has traveled from Shenzhen to San Francisco, empowering thousands of developers and producing hundreds of prototypes, all in a single day per city.

If you like working fast, this is where you belong.

- Claim free testnet AVAX
- Learn the basics of Solidity
- Write and compile a smart contract in Remix
- Deploy it to Avalanche Fuji
- Interact with your contract on-chain

- Leave with a public proof-of-work link you can share

### Who Should Attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

- Developers and engineering students
- Beginner Solidity developers
- Web3 and blockchain builders
- Hackathon participants
- Developers exploring Avalanche
- Anyone who wants their first hands-on smart contract deployment

You do not need prior Solidity or blockchain experience.

Just bring your laptop, browser, and curiosity.

### What You'll Build

During the workshop, you'll build and deploy a simple smart contract that stores a number on-chain and reads it back.

Along the way, you'll learn one of the most important Solidity concepts:

Storage vs Memory

You'll experience the difference between:

- Writing data on-chain and paying gas
- Reading blockchain state for free
- Temporary memory and permanent blockchain storage

By the end of the workshop, your contract will be live on Avalanche Fuji and publicly verifiable through the block explorer.

### Workshop Outcomes

Our goal is not just attendance.

We want participants to leave having actually used Avalanche.

Expected outcomes include:

- New developer wallets created
- Developers onboarded to Avalanche Fuji
- Smart contracts successfully deployed
- Public contract and transaction links generated
- Developers introduced to Avalanche Builder Hub, Academy and Docs
- New builders identified for future Team1 workshops and ecosystem opportunities

### About Team1

Team1 is a global network of builders, developers, creatives, and community members who grow Avalanche.

With 600+ members operating across 40 countries, Team1 drives the democratization and global adoption of Avalanche by onboarding new users and projects through local meetups, targeted workshops, exclusive side events, engaging content creation, and community-led initiatives.

By bridging online and offline communities, Team1 empowers grassroots innovation and expands the reach of Avalanche into new regions and cultures.

https://x.com/AvaxTeam1

What to bring

Laptop

Charger

No prior blockchain experience required

Everything during the workshop runs on Avalanche Fuji Testnet, so no real funds are required.

Come curious. Leave with your first smart contract deployed on Avalanche.

https://x.com/AvaxTeam1

## Bitcoin 101 for Developers & Curious Beginners \| Andheri, Mumbai

- Record: `india-luma-ual4wk7p`
- Source: [india-luma-events.json](sources/india-luma-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-26T06:15:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/ual4wk7p>

### About the event

How does Bitcoin work without a bank or a central server? And what actually happens when you send a bitcoin transaction?

Join Bitshala for a beginner-friendly workshop exploring how Bitcoin works under the hood. We'll break down the key ideas in simple language, follow a transaction through the network, and guide you through creating and sending one yourself.

You'll use Bitcoin's test network, so you can experiment without using real bitcoin. No prior coding or Bitcoin knowledge required.

### AGENDA

- Keys, addresses, and ownership: What a Bitcoin wallet does, how addresses work, and how you prove you can spend your bitcoin.
- How transactions work: How Bitcoin tracks individual pieces of bitcoin rather than a bank-style account balance, and how those pieces get spent and combined.
- A transaction's journey: What happens after you hit "send," how computers on the network check your transaction, and where it waits before being included in a block.
- Blocks and mining: How transactions are grouped into blocks, what miners do, and how the network agrees on a shared transaction history.
- Bitcoin's incentives and supply: Why miners earn rewards and fees, what a "halving" means, and how Bitcoin's 21 million supply limit works.
- Hands-on practice: With step-by-step guidance, build, sign, and send a transaction on Bitcoin's test network.

### WHO'S GUIDING

Led by the Bitshala Contributors. We are a community of Bitcoin developers and educators.

### WHAT TO EXPECT

- Level: Beginner-friendly.
- Format: An interactive workshop with explanations, room for questions, and a guided transaction exercise.
- Bring: A laptop and your curiosity.
- Experience needed: None. You don't need to know how to code.

### IS THIS FOR YOU?

This workshop is for you if you:

- Have used a Bitcoin wallet and wondered what happens behind the scenes.
- Are a developer looking for a starting point with Bitcoin.
- Are new to Bitcoin and prefer learning by doing.
- Want to understand how a network can work without one company running it.

Leave with a clearer picture of how Bitcoin works, and a test-network transaction you created yourself.

To connect with Bitcoiners in Mumbai, join the Signal group (https://signal.group/?utm_source=luma#CjQKIKC4IuqhHW1AQIB-44S0Dg4Um2BItqRBM_V3pzSAwRPoEhB7_H-3FcjjemIxbLkFtABe)

### About Bitshala

Bitshala (https://bitshala.org/) is a Bitcoin-focused education initiative where we help developers, designers, and curious builders learn by doing. We run cohorts, clubs, workshops, a hackerspace, and community programs that make it easier for people to explore, contribute to, and build on Bitcoin. Our focus is on hands-on learning, proof-of-work, and growing alongside a community of people who care about open technology, design, and the future of money.

If you'd like to explore more, check us out on:

- Discord (Online Community) (https://discord.com/invite/STeQFVEWf9)
- Cohorts Registration and Fellowship application portal (https://app.bitshala.org/)
- Twitter (Socials and Announcements) (https://x.com/bitshala_org)
- Luma (Events Calendar) (https://luma.com/bitshala)

### About the event

Think of the late-night bonding at a YC Hacker House or a top-tier AI research retreat. We are bringing together 15-20serious builders in Mumbai for an afternoon of high-trust networking and collaborative building.

No pitch decks. No VC speed-dating. No awkward small talk. We are engineering an environment where you actually get to know the person next to you by looking at their code, debating architecture, and helping each other get unstuck. If you are building AI agents, Web3 infrastructure, or consumer apps on Confidential AI/ Economy, this is your room.

### How We Network

The Problem Pitch:

Come prepared to share what you're building, the problem you're facing, and what you're stuck on right now. Keep it short and concrete, no polished elevator pitches needed.

The Room Helps:

After each pitch, the audience can jump in with ideas, relevant experience, introductions, or potential solutions. If you've faced the same problem before, share what worked (or didn't).

We don't want forced networking, writing exercises, or people splitting off into groups. The goal is simply to put interesting problems in front of smart people and let the conversation happen naturally.

Dinner/Drinks Post-Session:

After the session, we'll head somewhere nearby for food and drinks. That's where you can continue the conversations, meet people one-on-one, and explore ideas that came up during the session.

### Who is this for?

- Builders who want to find technical collaborators, not just "connections."
- Engineers, designers, and product hackers actively shipping on NEAR or AI.
- People who prefer deep, 1-on-1 technical debates over loud, crowded rooms.

## Bitcoin Wallets: Keys, Transactions, and the Mempool \| Chandigarh

- Record: `india-luma-mlg5zv5y`
- Source: [india-luma-events.json](sources/india-luma-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-27T06:30:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/mlg5zv5y>

### About the event

When you click "Send," your wallet doesn't transfer money, it broadcasts a cryptographic signature directly to a global, ownerless network.

Join us for a deep dive into the inner workings of Bitcoin wallets! Whether you're a developer, a curious Bitcoiner, or someone wanting to understand what happens under the hood when you click "Send," this meetup is for you.

We will break down how wallets manage your secret keys, how transactions are constructed and signed, and how they navigate the mempool to reach finality on the blockchain.

### AGENDA

- Public vs. Private Keys: How cryptographic key pairs prove ownership.
- Seed Phrases & HD Wallets: How 12 to 24 words can restore all your funds across multiple addresses.
- Key Management Best Practices: Hot wallets vs. Cold storage and multisig setups.
- UTXO Model: How Bitcoin tracks ownership using Unspent Transaction Outputs instead of balance accounts.
- Transaction Anatomy: Inputs, Outputs, ScriptPubKey, and Digital Signatures.
- Fee Estimation & RBF: Understanding mining fees and Replace-By-Fee (RBF) mechanics.
- What is the Mempool?: How nodes receive, validate, and queue unconfirmed transactions.
- Fee Rates & Priority: How miners select transactions based on satoshis per vByte (sat/vB).
- Congestion & Confirmation: What happens during high-traffic periods and how to navigate stuck transactions.

### WHO'S GUIDING

Led by Bitshala educators and open-source builders. Our sessions are led by active community members who build open-source tools, study the Bitcoin protocol, and advocate for transparent, open software.

### WHAT TO EXPECT

- Difficulty: Beginner level. Designed for absolute newcomers.
- Zero Fluff: No sales pitches, no trading talk, and no corporate slides. Just pure peer-to-peer technical literacy.

### IS THIS FOR YOU?

- You are curious about how money and technology intersect.
- You want to understand how Bitcoin works under the hood rather than follow market trends.
- You prefer clear, logical explanations over complex jargon.
- You enjoy asking foundational questions in a welcoming, hands-on environment.

Coding experience not required. Intellectual curiosity about peer-to-peer technology is.

You will leave this session with a clear, grounded understanding of how value travels from a local secret key to permanent block confirmation.

### About Bitshala

Bitshala (https://bitshala.org/) is a Bitcoin-focused education initiative where we help developers, designers, and curious builders learn by doing. We run cohorts, clubs, workshops, a hackerspace, and community programs that make it easier for people to explore, contribute to, and build on Bitcoin. Our focus is on hands-on learning, proof-of-work, and growing alongside a community of people who care about open technology, design, and the future of money.

If you'd like to explore more, check us out on:

- Discord (Online Community) (https://discord.com/invite/STeQFVEWf9)

## Bitshala BOSS Summit 2026 \| Jaipur \| 26 Oct - 31 Oct

- Record: `india-luma-bitshalaboss`

### Bitshala BOSS (Bitcoin Open-Source Software) Summit 2026 | Jaipur

Join us for 6 days of fun, work, collaboration, and deep learning at the frontiers of Bitcoin open-source software design and development.

### What's happening

Expect a highly collaborative residency with sessions, workshops, demos, open discussions, and hands-on building time.

You'll get to:

- Learn what's happening at the frontiers of Bitcoin OSS development and design
- Meet developers and designers working on active Bitcoin projects
- Connect with product builders and educators taking Bitcoin to more people
- Share demos, prototypes, workshops, and project ideas
- Find collaborators for GitHub repos, Figma files, personal projects, or products
- Spend time with fellow builders through games, sports, bonfires, walks, treks, and sightseeing

Whether you're contributing to open-source software, designing better Bitcoin user experiences, building educational content, or working on a product, BOSS Summit is designed to help you meet the right people and move your work forward.

### Timelines

- Monday, 26 Oct
  - Check-in
  - 16:00 : Welcome & introductions
- Tuesday, 27 Oct - Thursday, 29 Oct (10:00 - 17:00)
  - Sessions, Workshops, Open Slots, Demos, Project discussions and Collaboration time
  - Evenings will include fun games, sports, bonfires, and informal hangouts.
- Friday, 30 Oct - Saturday, 31 Oct
  - Bitmela
- Sunday, 1 Nov
  - Checkout by 11:00 AM

### Who Should Apply

We have limited seats for:

- Bitcoin developers
- Product designers
- UX/UI designers
- Bitcoin educators
- Product builders
- People actively working on Bitcoin projects, tools, content, or education

Seats are sponsored by Bitshala, so please make a strong application to help us understand what you're working on and how you hope to contribute during the residency.

### Bring Your Work

Have an active GitHub repo, a Figma file, a workshop idea, a product prototype, or a personal project?

Bring it along.

BOSS Summit is a place to share work-in-progress, find collaborators, get feedback, jam on ideas, and build alongside others who care deeply about Bitcoin and open-source software.

### Bringing a Family Member or Friend

If you're planning to bring a family member or friend, we'll connect you with the venue provider or Airbnb options.

You can directly pay for their stay and meals with the provider.

### Apply to Get Invited

BOSS Summit has limited invited seats for Bitcoin developers, designers, educators, and builders.

If you're excited to learn, contribute, build, teach, design, or collaborate around Bitcoin open-source software, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and tell us what you're building.

For any queries drop a mail to contact@bitshala.org

### Glimpse of Our Last BOSS Summit

Dharmshala - Summer 2026

Catch a glimpse of the energy, collaboration, and moments from our last BOSS Summit in Dharmshala - from deep work sessions and demos to bonfires, games, and community bonding.

Explore more here: The official BOSS Summit After-Movie and Article (https://x.com/bitshala_org/status/2049831566827008161)

### About Bitshala

Bitshala (https://bitshala.org/) is a Bitcoin-focused education initiative where we help developers, designers, and curious builders learn by doing. We run cohorts, clubs, workshops, a hackerspace, and community programs that make it easier for people to explore, contribute to, and build on Bitcoin. Our focus is on hands-on learning, proof-of-work, and growing alongside a community of people who care about open technology, design, and the future of money.

Cypherpunk Congress is coming to India!

### The first batch of highly-curated speakers are here

Curatorial note: we assemble speakers on intersection between digital rights, FOSS, decentralisation & cryptography.

They propose practical solutions for global challenges from polarisation in social media to raise of dictatorships. Challenge internet shutdowns, abuse of digital identity, & attacks on encryption. With proven track record from @EFF (https://x.com/EFF) to @brave (https://x.com/brave).

Welcome to Mumbai!

### Lasting cultural phenomenon

Focusing on values, active political stance, and cutting-edge research will help Ethereum become a cultural & resilient to change phenomenon.

watch aftermovie: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=97-qkXRmMlk

expect phenomenal lineup [Congress #2 example]

We are talking not only about the existence of privacy-preservation dapps, but Free & Open-source software development, support for free speech and whistleblowers around the world, helping marginalized people get access to the decolonial money system, safe & empowered tech, and last but not least - diverse and active communities of care.

Supporting privacy developers

Roman Storm Congress #2 opening https://youtu.be/XKJ1ZJrkKWA?si=GGrhiF5TOZcfjUqy&t=811

### Connecting web2 + web3

Vitalik Buterin + Naomi Brockwell fireside https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5At5_GiQNEA

### Ethereum Social Layer (ESL)

It is being formed before our eyes - an active ecosystem of thousands of thinkers, developers, analysts, human-rights DAOs, coordinators, and even ravers. Inspired by cypherpunks of the past, they create a foundation for the digital community of the future (explore our Cyherpunk personas (https://mirror.xyz/0x0f1F3DAf416B74DB3DE55Eb4D7513a80F4841073/u4ELDt0YkpCe272kD2f5kTThJsILg1pgaOeBsTSGV0I) article). Based on permissionless & censorship-resistance ideology. Follow Paul-Dylan Ennis (https://x.com/post_polar_/status/1813275641954877709) on ESL.

### Activation

The debut Ethereum Cypherpunk Congress assembles an active part of Ethereum. These people and organizations want to stand at the foundations of the unstoppable socio-techno-cultural movement.

Special rituals help us to share Cypherpunk culture & build care for each other.

They are activists, developers, cryptographers, ethical investors, philosophers, and researchers who are changing the possibilities for Ethereum on the path to freedom.

Hackathon track

Events for developers are critical activation points behind any cultural change. Every protocol from Aztec to Ethereum needs devs to build on top of it & deliver decentralized, permissionless & privacy-enhancing applications. We invited current privacy hackathon devs to reflect on their experience.

Women in web3 privacy track

Diversity in the web3 industry is a critical challenge, let alone in the privacy market. Let's discuss how we can be more open, diverse & inclusive to different opinions and opportunities.

Activation track

We want everyone to feel, use and contribute to practical privacy tooling. So we will showcase existing tools empowering your journey in decentralized world: Fileverse (http://fileverse.io), Rotki (http://rotki.com), Fluidkey (http://fluidkey.com), Radicle, GnosisVPN.

Stunning merch delivered by Coinmandeer

### High-level agenda

- craft conditions needed to overcome challenges mapped in "Make Ethereum Cypherpunk again" essay
- present Ethereum Privacy Ecosystem (https://docs.web3privacy.info/research/ethereum-privacy-ecosystem/) and its key players
- explore socio-cultural conditions re-wiring degens into cypher-activists
- build a mainstream culture around cypherpunk - make it an open and inclusive movement
- remind of the origins of Ethereum ethos
- articulate balance between open-source culture & financial sustainability behind projects
- map the way to onboard 100K developers & 10M users experiencing safe Ethereum-centric privacy tech

Contribute to the development of the cypherpunk culture of Ethereum. Everyone will be welcome here, from activists defending the rights of developers to degens who finally want to find a strong meaning in life.

### EIP Hub @ Devcon 8 India

Where Ethereum Standards Come Together

The EIP Hub is a collaborative space dedicated to Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs), ERC standards, protocol upgrades, and standards adoption. Whether you're a first-time contributor, protocol researcher, client developer, standards author, application builder, enterprise architect, or simply curious about how Ethereum evolves, the EIP Hub is your place to learn, collaborate, and contribute.

Over four days, the hub will host talks, workshops, office hours, roundtables, live demonstrations, and networking sessions focused on the complete journey of an Ethereum standard - from understanding the EIP process to protocol development, application standards, and enterprise adoption.

### What to expect

- Learn how Ethereum's standards process works
- Meet EIP editors, authors, client teams, and researchers
- Join EIP Office Hours and protocol discussions
- Explore upcoming network upgrades and Meta EIPs
- Discover the latest ERCs and application standards
- Participate in workshops and specification reviews
- Connect with tooling projects and enterprise builders
- Experience live EIPsInsight dashboards and protocol updates

Detailed event coming soon!

Whether you're looking to write your first EIP, discuss the next protocol upgrade, showcase a new ERC, or connect with fellow contributors, the EIP Hub is designed to be the home for Ethereum standards throughout Devcon.

Explore. Innovate. Participate.

Note: The EIP Hub is only accessible to Devcon 8 ticket holders. A valid Devcon ticket is required to enter.

FAEZEH GHAVIDEL, Multidisciplinary Artist, Author & Curator. Faezeh is a multidisciplinary artist working across painting, digital media, motion, sound, and text. Her work explores emotional and psychological states through a visual language shaped by intimacy, vulnerability, transformation, and the complexities of human experience. She has created over 300 physical artworks alongside an extensive body of motion-based works, sometimes accompanied by her own music.

Her work has been exhibited internationally across Dubai, Beijing, Paris, Istanbul, and the United States, including New York's Times Square and the Oculus at the World Trade Center, and is held in private collections internationally. She is also a writer and musician, allowing image, sound, and text to intersect within her artistic language. https://www.instagram.com/faa.videl & https://www.linkedin.

BAIBA BROKA, General Counsel at ZIGChain and ZIG Markets. Baiba is General Counsel at ZIGChain and ZIG Markets and founder of Grand Stream, a consultancy company providing legal and crypto licensing services in the UAE and Europe. In Web3 since 2014, she brings traditional capital markets on-chain within the ZIG ecosystem, including Zamanat, a Shariah-compliant RWA platform, and its Zamanat CEIG Fund in DIFC. She has over 20 years of academic and research experience, teaching financial law and international transactions. She advised ministers and served as Minister of Justice.

Baiba is an ad honorem member of UNIDROIT, she contributed to its 2023 Principles on Digital Assets and Private Law. Passionate about democratizing capital markets and financial inclusion, she believes everyone deserves better ways to manage money, invest, and build their future. https://www.instagram.com/bbaiba1 & https://www.linkedin.

NICOLE PURIN, Legal & Regulatory Advisor | Financial Services, Digital Assets & AI. A Solicitor of England & Wales, Nicole has extensive experience advising on complex regulatory, governance and compliance matters across multiple jurisdictions, with particular expertise in digital assets, payments, financial crime, cybersecurity and AI. https://www.instagram.com/contessa_lifestyle/ & https://www.

linkedin.

BRYAN TOROMO, Senior Software Engineer | Financial Systems & AI. Bryan is a senior software engineer working across financial platforms and applied AI. He is also co-founder of Waingoo, a conversational shopping platform serving the Kenyan market through WhatsApp and Telegram. His content explores emerging technology through an engineer's lens: how systems work, what new tools can deliver, and how to test their limits.

He is exploring how human specialists can retain the understanding needed to judge and direct AI-produced software as systems evolve, with the longer-term aim of preparing human expertise for the possibility of artificial superintelligence (ASI). https://www.instagram.com/bryan_toromo/ & https://www.linkedin.

### About the event

If commercial space flights land on Mars tomorrow, what would you build to create the Martian city?

[APPLICATIONS CLOSED]

Join GirlsWhoML (https://www.girlswhoml.com/) and PhysicsX (https://www.physicsx.ai/) for an evening hackathon in London to tackle the first human landing on Mars, supported by Cursor. You arrive on an empty, rust-red planet with no city, no roads, and no infrastructure. What do you build first?

You'll design and prototype one core system for the Martian city, across three tracks: Architecture, Vehicles, and Life Support. Every build should combine engineering, machine learning, or 3D modelling.

The window is short, but that's the point: see how far you can push what's possible in a single evening. Mentors will be on the floor throughout, your work will be reviewed by a panel of industry judges, and every participant gets Cursor credits supported by Francisco Terpolilli, Cursor's EU Ambassador and Regional Leader.

Bring a team of 2-3, or turn up solo and we'll help you find a crew, at our team formation session. Women, non-binary, and allies are all welcome.

Prizes provided by PhysicsX (https://www.physicsx.ai/), including career coaching and mentorship opportunities, to be announced.

Bring your curiosity, your laptop, and your ambition. The city starts with you.

### Schedule

5:30pm - launch pad

6:00pm - mission briefing

6:20pm - ignition

8:00pm - mid mission check

8:30pm - code freeze

8:38pm - demos

9:30pm - judging

9:45pm - close

Thank you so much for the incredible response to this hackathon. We've been genuinely overwhelmed (in the best way!) by the interest, which far exceeds our venue's capacity.

Because space is limited, we've had to carefully curate a group that reflects our community and fits the hack's brief. With so many strong applications, this was a difficult process.

If you don't receive a spot this time, please know it comes down to capacity and fit for this specific event not a judgment on your talent or potential. Thank you again for your enthusiasm and for taking the time to apply.

### About the event

The official Liberland meetup of the week

Join us for a special edition of Tech Tuesdays in the heart of Times Square during Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition, September 10 to 19, 2026.

As the United Nations General Assembly convenes in New York, we are bringing together builders, founders, developers, investors, creatives and impact-focused professionals for an evening of meaningful conversation and high-quality networking.

Liberland at Times Square

This is the official meetup spot for Liberlanders and supporters of Liberland during Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition. If you are in New York for the week, this is where the Liberland community gathers. Come meet fellow citizens, supporters and the curious, and hear where the project stands heading into 2027.

Liberland has been part of Blockchain Week for years, and President Vít Jedlička returns to the program again this year. Whether you hold a Liberland passport, follow the project, or are hearing about it for the first time, you are welcome here.

### What to Expect

Multiple high-level panels on emerging technology and how blockchain creates real-world impact: sustainability, transparent aid, AI and energy, digital public infrastructure, space technology, and fashion innovation.

Relaxed, vibrant networking in one of the most energetic locations in the world.

A prime spot in iconic Times Square, steps from our three-screen marquee on the front of the Hard Rock, which runs throughout the event.

Whether you are deep in Web3 or simply blockchain-curious, this event is free and open to everyone.

### Details

Date: Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Time: 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM

Location: Legends Bar and the New York Room, Hard Rock Cafe Times Square, Manhattan, NY

Free to attend. RSVP here so we can plan the room.

The Rest of the Week

Tech Tuesdays is one of 12+ official events across the 10-day program, September 10 to 19. The week includes the Orbital Runway opening night on the 10th, the two-day flagship conference on the 16th and 17th, BitcoinPalooza as the official after party, the Washington Elite Investment Summit and Gala on the 18th, and the Pause the World for Peace concert in Times Square on the 19th.

Full program and tickets at blockchainweek.ai (https://blockchainweek.ai)

### About the event

We've got a great Crypto Mondays Stamford/Greenwich on September 15 in Stamford, CT featuring Alden Knowlton, Senior Director - Economic Policy at Invariant, and special guest, Stamford Mayor Caroline Simmons.

Alden, based in Washington DC, focuses on navigating the intersection of technology, financial services, and economic policy.

Previously, Alden led Democratic lobbying and political strategy at Coinbase, where she secured historic bipartisan support for digital asset legislation and built the company's PAC and political engagement infrastructure.

Before that, she served as Vice President of Legislative and Political Affairs at the Mortgage Bankers Association, where she delivered key policy wins and developed one of the industry's most effective PAC and grassroots programs. Earlier in her career, Alden held leadership roles in political consulting and advocacy, managing multimillion-dollar PAC efforts and providing strategic counsel to congressional campaigns and national trade associations.

We are also pleased to welcome Mayor Caroline Simmons, who will discuss Stamford's growing innovation and technology ecosystem - and what that growth could mean for businesses, investors, entrepreneurs, and the broader Fairfield County economy.

Why Attend?

- Gain firsthand insights into the latest U.S. crypto policy and regulatory landscape from one of Washington's leading digital asset policy experts.
- Explore how policy and innovation are shaping the future of digital assets, stablecoins, and tokenization.
- Hear from Alden, a distinguished speaker offering perspectives on the industry's next chapter.
- Hear from Mayor Simmons regarding the exciting innovation ecosystem in Stamford.
- Participate in an interactive audience Q&A.
- Network with Connecticut's growing community of leaders in crypto, fintech, AI, quantum computing, venture, and capital markets.

### Tencent Cloud AI CAN DO IT Hackathon Singapore 2026

Co-hosted by Tencent Cloud and AI Singapore, the AI CAN DO IT Tencent Cloud Hackathon Singapore 2026 brings together industry expertise, leading AI technologies, and academic talent to empower the next generation of AI innovators.

Participants will develop practical Agentic AI solutions using Tencent Cloud's latest AI products, including CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy and Miora, to tackle real world business challenges contributed by leading organizations across industries.

This year's Hackathon features five industry tracks.

### Five Industry Tracks. Real Challenges. Real Impact

Banking Track - DBS

Challenge: Direct Conversational Transaction Agent (DCTA)

Real Estate Track - Keppel

Challenge: AI HARVEST - Turning Expert Know-How into Reusable Intelligence

FinTech Track - Aspire

Challenge: The Internal Brain - Building a Context-Aware Enterprise Knowledge System with RBAC, Security Logging & Audit Trail

Digital Native Track - Ryde

Challenge: Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution System

Healthcare Track - NTU LKCMedicine

Challenge 1: AI Grandma Knows Best: Intelligent Self-Triage and Care Navigation

Challenge 2: AI Healthier Every Day: Intelligent Support for Long-Term Self-Care

Each track is supported by industry organizations contributing real-world challenge statements and participating in the evaluation and judging of solutions.

From industry challenges to hands-on AI workshops and demos, participants will have the opportunity to build, experiment, and innovate with Tencent Cloud's AI technologies.

### Hackathon Journey

16 Sep - Kick-off Event

16 Oct - Submission Deadline

23 Oct - Finalists Announcement

3 Nov - Demo Day

### Prizes & Participant Benefits

All participants will receive CodeBuddy and WorkBuddy credits to support their hackathon journey. Top-performing teams at the Demo Day will receive:

First Prize - SGD 10,000

Second Prize - SGD 5,000

Third Prize - SGD 2,000

YouTube: https://youtube.com/live/RFz_N8K2ZHA?feature=share

Sign Up Your Team for the Hackathon:

### Colosseum Hackathonの「勝ち方」を、経験者から学ぶ。

アイデアは、どう選ぶのか。

限られた期間で、どこまで作り込むのか。

そして、審査員に何を伝えればいいのか。

今回は、

- LootGO Co-Founder Yuki
- Daiko Co-Founder zkYuki

Colosseum Hackathonの入賞経験者を迎え、実践的なPlaybookを共有します。

単なる体験談ではなく、

「何を作るか」

「どこに時間を使うか」

「どう見せるか」

「何が勝敗を分けるのか」

といった、Hackathonに挑戦するBuilderが知っておきたいポイントを、Fireside Chatとレクチャー形式で掘り下げます。

### 開催日時

2026年9月16日(水) 20:00

Superteam Japan Discord

### 登壇者情報

hax (@256hax (https://x.com/256hax))

Co-Country Lead & CTO, Superteam Japan

https://x.com/SuperteamJapan

zkYuki (@zkyuki_Ditto (https://x.com/zkyuki_Ditto))

Co-Founder, Daiko

https://x.com/DaikoAI

Yuki (@yuki__app (https://x.com/yuki__app))

Co-Founder, LootGO

https://x.com/lootgo_official

### イベント参加が初めての方へ

イベントにスムーズに参加するため、以下のSTEPに沿って準備をお願いします。3分ほどで完了します。

STEP 1：Luma（ルマ）で参加登録をする

まずは、このページで申し込みを完了させましょう。

右上の [ログイン] を押し、Googleアカウント等でログインします。

その後、このページで [参加登録] ボタンを押せば完了です！

登録したメールアドレスに案内が届きます。

STEP 2：会場「Discord（ディスコード）」の準備

今回のイベント会場は、スマホやPCで使えるコミュニケーションアプリ「Discord」になります。

参加URL： Discordサーバーに参加 (https://discord.com/invite/stjp?utm_source=luma)

スマホで参加の方 事前にアプリをインストールしておくと、当日の参加がとてもスムーズです。

iPhoneの方（App Store） (https://apps.apple.com/jp/app/discord-%E4%B8%80%E7%B7%92%E3%81%AB%E3%81%97%E3%82%83%E3%81%B9%E3%81%A3%E3%81%A6%E9%81%8A%E3%82%93%E3%81%A7%E9%9B%86%E3%81%BE%E3%82%8D%E3%81%86/id985746746?utm_source=luma)

Androidの方（Google Play） (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.discord&hl=ja&utm_source=luma)

PCで参加の方 アプリを入れなくても、いつものブラウザ（ChromeやSafariなど）でそのまま開けます。

STEP 3：イベント参加と「認証（Verify）」

アカウントの準備ができたら、以下の手順でDiscordへお入りください。

「人間であること」の確認（認証）： Discordに入った直後は、まだ中身（チャンネル）が見えない設定になっています。セキュリティのため、以下のURLをクリックして認証を行ってください。

ここをクリックして認証ページを開く (https://discord.com/channels/1106919982224384081/1111570304708390975?utm_source=luma)

画面に表示される指示（対象の文字にあう絵文字を選択）に従うと、すべてのチャンネルが見えるようになります。

## 2026 AI Web3 投資：如何打造一人 AI 研究團隊

- Record: `luma-crypto-EjoD89X0CHsHeV7`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-16T11:00:00.000Z

### About the event

AI 工具經常聽到，但到底怎樣用在「投資」上面？

學得再多功能，如果最後不能夠變成你的資產，其實完全沒有用。而 AI 最能夠落地的地方，一定是投資。

以前一間機構要一隊人才做得到的研究，今日一個人加一部電腦就做得到。

這一晚會講三件事

① 如何建立你的第一個 AI 員工

打造一個 '有記憶' 的 AI ，24/7 隨時候命的私人員工。

② 如何解決 AI 有幻覺的問題

AI 最擅長的，是把不確定的事寫得好像很肯定。你不敢用它的結論去做決定，問題就在這裡。

解決這個問題，AI 的產出才算真的可以用 - - 否則做得越快，錯得越快。

③ 了解完整 AI Full Investment Team 的能力

一個員工，其實只是開始。

最後我會給你看一支完整的 AI Investment Team：情報收集、深度研究、風險檢查各自分工。

你會看到差距在哪裡，也會知道由「一個員工」走到「一支團隊」，中間實際上需要什麼。

適合邊個

對 crypto / 投資有興趣、想學識用 AI 幫自己做判斷嘅你 - - 完全新手都歡迎。

費用：完全免費

時間：9月16號 晚上7點 - 9點

（建議帶備個人電腦，方便一起實戰操作）

關於講者

Matthew - CFA / FRM,前對沖基金投資總監, Chainlab 創辦人。

## Crossing the Fiat–Crypto Boundary: Basel III, Compliance and Control

- Record: `luma-crypto-AMhTnCWXTOkbooi`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-17T08:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/1czivcbs>

### About the event

UPDATE: due to overwhelming demand, this event is now at capacity! Please register anyway to join the waiting list and we'll notify you if a seat is available. Thank you for your interest!

Hong Kong has moved beyond the question of whether crypto should be regulated. The harder question is how banks, securities firms, exchanges, and stablecoin payment providers make different regulatory regimes and control systems work together.

Basel III shapes how banks approach cryptoasset exposure. Securities and virtual asset firms face their own licensing, custody, and market-conduct obligations. Across the chain, compliance teams must detect financial crime using customer records, fiat transactions, wallet activity, and blockchain data that rarely sit in the same system.

One panel. Every side of the fiat-crypto boundary.

These speakers have sat on every side of the table: regulating financial markets, leading compliance inside banks and securities firms, operating global crypto exchanges, advising law enforcement, and applying those rules to stablecoin payments.

- Angelina Kwan, CEO at Stratford Finance Limited, formerly Global COO at BitMEX and HashKey Group, HKEX, and SFC.
- Avina Lobo, Regulatory Compliance Lead at Reap, formerly Animoca Brands and Bitget
- Debra Au, Co-chair of Global Coalition Fighting for Financial Crime APAC and Cyber Crime Policing Advisory Panel Member at Hong Kong Police Force. Previously Head of Financial Crime at HSBC HK, Societe Generale, and DBS.
- Lorraine Li, Head of Compliance at Mirae Asset Securities. Previously Head of Compliance Advisory at HSBC HK.
- Moderated by Teodora Irimia, Senior Account Executive, Flagright

Together, they will examine:

- Who monitors a transaction that passes through a bank, exchange, stablecoin provider, and self-hosted wallet?
- What changes when an established financial group acquires or partners with a crypto business?
- When is de-risking prudent, and when does it push activity beyond the regulated perimeter?
- What controls and evidence should regulators expect when monitoring spans both fiat and on-chain activity?

A practitioner-led discussion for people working in virtual assets, regulatory policy, compliance, payments, securities, and institutional treasury.

### AGENDA

04:00 PM: Doors open, registration, and coffee refreshments

04:45 PM: Panel discussion: Crossing the Fiat-Crypto Boundary: Basel III, Compliance and Control

- Audience Q&A and moderated discussion
- Live Demo

05:30 PM: Networking

7:00 PM: Close

[Notice: there may be photos taken during this event, please advise the host if you do not wish to have your photo shared.]

Members will gather in London during Fashion Week for an intimate evening with Rita Qaranbach, the London based Lebanese designer whose work has sparked global conversations around fashion, culture, and representation.

Rita's designs have reached millions online, including the viral Spider Man sari worn by creator Atifa Arshad and Zainab Jiwa's widely celebrated Devil Wears Prada look.

As fashion continues to evolve beyond runways and magazines, designers today are shaping culture in real time. The pieces that resonate most are often those that tell a deeper story about identity, heritage, belonging, and the communities they represent.

Topics on the table include:

- How fashion became one of the internet's most powerful forms of storytelling
- Building a distinctive creative voice in a crowded industry
- Representation, identity, and designing for communities that have historically been overlooked
- The cultural impact of viral fashion moments
- What luxury brands still get wrong about authenticity
- The future of fashion, craftsmanship, and cultural influence

Expect a room filled with people building brands, telling stories, shaping culture, and contributing to the future of fashion from a range of perspectives.

### About Rita Qaranbach

A London based Lebanese fashion designer whose work sits at the intersection of fashion, culture, and storytelling.

Many people discovered Rita through the viral fashion moments that captured millions online, including the Spider Man sari worn by Atifa Arshad and Zainab Jiwa's Devil Wears Prada look. But behind those moments is a designer who has spent years exploring how fashion can express identity, heritage, and representation in a way that feels both contemporary and deeply personal.

## The Software Factory with SuperPlane & Elastic - When Agents Build, Ship, and Fix Your Code

- Record: `luma-crypto-EdxcyBvKjWGpHRo`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

### About the event

Software factories are here. AI agents write code, open PRs, run tests, deploy to production, and respond to incidents - all without waiting for a human to click a button.

Join SuperPlane and Elastic for an evening where engineering leaders, platform teams, and SREs explore what it actually takes to run a software factory: how agents ship code, how Elastic monitors what happens in production, and how SuperPlane orchestrates the full loop from commit → deploy to incident to fix. SuperPlane is the agent orchestrator that turns your tools into a software factory. Elastic is the observability engine that tells you what's happening inside it.

This is an unconference, you bring the topics, we bring the structure (and drinks). Come with opinions about how far you'd let agents go.

Date: Thursday, September 17th from 6:00-9:00 PM

Location: Elastic NYC Office

1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training Room

New York, NY 10001

Some topics we would discuss:

- How much autonomy should agents have in production?
- Building the feedback loop: deploy → observe → respond → learn
- Agents that fix what agents broke - is that a loop or a spiral?
- What does "human in the loop" actually mean when agents ship 10x faster?
- Observability as the control plane for your software factory
- From Kibana alert to automated rollback - what's your threshold?
- The trust problem: when do you stop reviewing agent PRs?

### Format

- Topics proposed by attendees at the beginning
- Sessions run in small groups (~5-7 people)
- 30 minutes of facilitated discussion per session
- Open participation and movement between sessions encouraged

### Schedule

- 6:00 - 6:30 PM → Arrival, food & drinks, networking
- 6:30 - 6:50 PM → Welcome + software factories w/ Elastic & Superplane
- 6:50 - 7:00 PM → Topic proposals & voting
- 7:00 - 7:30 PM → Session 1
- 7:30 - 7:40 PM → Short break
- 7:40 - 8:10 PM → Session 2
- 8:10 - 8:20 PM → Short break
- 8:20 - 8:50 PM → Session 3
- 8:50 - 9:00 PM → Wrap-up & key takeaways
- 9:00 PM → Closing

Coming up: ElasticON NYC

Join us October 8 for a free day of hands-on learning, expert insights, and real-world AI, search, observability, and security sessions. Register for fre (https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/new-york-city)e (https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/new-york-city?utm_source=luma&utm_medium=event_page&utm_campaign=elasticon_nyc_2026&utm_content=superplane_meetup_sep17).

### About SuperPlane

SuperPlane (https://superplane.com/) Software Factory platform that transforms software delivery from a collection of manual tasks into an orchestrated, AI-powered production system. It coordinates AI agents, developers, infrastructure, and operational tools to build, test, deploy, and maintain software with speed, consistency, and governance.

### About Elastic

Elastic (https://www.elastic.co/?utm_source=luma) is the observability stack behind high-velocity engineering teams. With Elasticsearch, Kibana, and the rest of Elastic Stack, engineers, SREs and platform engineers get real-time visibility into logs, metrics, traces, and security events correlated in one place, not scattered across tools. As release cadence increases with the adoption of software factories, Elastic keeps you in control of what's running and why.

### About the Event

The Official After-Party of Blockchain Week

Date: Thursday, September 17, 2026

Venue: Sugar Mouse NYC, 47 3rd Ave, New York, NY 10003

Doors Open: 7:00 PM

Programming Until: Midnight

Age Restriction: 18+ with government-issued photo ID

Most crypto events stop at panels. This one doesn't.

BitcoinPalooza is New York City's premier celebration of Bitcoin culture, returning for its fourth year. We close Day Two of the flagship Blockchain Week conference with an immersive evening of live music, curated art, fashion, and conversation - right in the heart of Times Square.

No lanyards, no stuffy receptions - just a genuine cultural night for the crypto community and beyond.

### What's Happening

- Live Music - Performances by NYC's own crypto‑degen band The Coinheads, alongside recording artists Emily Lazar and others.
- Fashion Show - Presented by artist and creative director Alejandro Glatt.
- Visual Art - Curated works displayed throughout the venue, featured across Blockchain Week venues for all ten days.
- Conversations - Featuring industry leaders and thought provocateurs:
  - Karla Ballard
  - Lou Kerner
  - Brian J. Esposito
  - Thomas Walls

More announcements to come from our newly appointed curator, Lara Moreno, whose sole mission is to make this feel like a true cultural night, not a conference reception.

### Who's in the Room

Founders, investors, diplomats, artists, and musicians - all in New York for UN General Assembly week, gathering under one roof without the formalities.

### Tickets

General Admission is $89. VIP Access is $249 and adds priority entry from 6:30 PM, lounge access, reserved seating, meet-and-greet opportunities, limited-edition merch and a welcome drink.

Capacity is limited and the room is smaller than the interest in it. Prices rise as September gets closer.

All attendees must be 18+ and present valid government‑issued photo ID.

### Call for Artists, Musicians, and Designers

Submissions for the 2026 edition are open until Friday, September 4.

Send links to your work to lara@bitcoinpalooza.nyc with a short note describing what you'd like to present. No formal proposal required - every submission receives a reply.

### Good to Know

- No Blockchain Week conference pass is required. This event is ticketed separately and open to everyone.
- A BitcoinPalooza ticket admits you to September 17 only. The full twelve‑event program is available at blockchainweek.ai/program (https://blockchainweek.ai/program).
- Blockchain Week - UNGA Edition is an independent initiative and is not affiliated with the United Nations.

### Full Lineup & Details

Visit https://bitcoinpalooza.nyc for the complete lineup and ongoing updates.

### Press & Media Kit

Download materials at https://bitcoinpalooza.nyc/press

We look forward to celebrating with you on September 17 - see you in Times Square.

## Robot Hackathon: Fine Motor Skills

- Record: `luma-crypto-ojo8Xh2wktYW9od`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-18T13:00:00.000Z

### About the Event

Build physical AI applications with real robot arms @ Viam!

We're excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm and support from Viam experts throughout.

No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI and some software experience.

Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.

What You'll Build

Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam and a real robot arm.

Each team will have access to:

- UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101)
- Linux compute machine
- RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm)
- Webcams
- A free Viam (https://docs.viam.com/what-is-viam/) account

We'll provide blocks, cups, pens, paper, and other objects for your robot to interact with, or bring something you'd like to experiment with.

Please bring your own laptop.

Challenges

Accepted participants can select from predefined projects or bring your own idea.

1) Benchmark ideas: pick one of five tasks and get scored on it.
- Charger plugging: Sub-centimeter precision, occlusion at the moment of contact
- Pouring liquid into a cup: Continuous control; a spill is a visible failure
- Recycling sort: Perception in clutter
- Egg transfer: Force control; failure is unambiguous and dramatic
- Jenga pull: Precision plus force feedback; the tower falling ends your run
2) Open: bring your own idea and get judged on ambition and execution.
- Ideas from past events: playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, setting a table, folding clothes.

### Prizes

We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. Winning teams take home robot arms:

- Gold: UFactory Lite6 arm + $5,000 in Viam credits
- Silver: Seeed Studio reBot Arm B601-RS + $2,500 in Viam credits
- Bronze: SO-101 arm + $1,000 in Viam credits

Please bring your own laptop. We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (https://www.viam.com/viam-101/?utm_medium=luma&utm_source=finemotorskills&utm_campaign=vmrk-luma-finemotorskills-viam101-learn&utm_content=lp_viam101) (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even if you only go through the first lessons, it will help you get the hang of things quickly.

### Schedule

Friday, September 18

9:00 AM: Check-in and breakfast

9:30 AM: Kickoff: Welcome & crash course on building with Viam

10:30 AM: Teams and hardware

11:00 AM: Hacking begins

1:00 PM: Lunch

6:00 PM: Dinner

9:00 PM: Hard close: Robots power down, doors close (no overnight hacking)

Saturday, September 19

9:00 AM: Doors open, breakfast

9:30 AM: Hacking resumes

12:30 PM: Lunch

3:30 PM: Demos and drinks

5:00 PM: Awards

6:00 PM: Event concludes

What Skills You Need

No robotics experience required, but you should be comfortable with:

- Coding: Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C++
- Linux: Using SSH and running basic terminal commands
- JSON: Reading and editing configuration files
- Git: Basic workflows so your team can build together
- Bonus: knowing how to plug in a pre-trained vision model (like YOLO or OpenCV) to help the robot see and identify objects (not required)

Before the Event

We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (https://www.viam.com/viam-101/?utm_medium=luma&utm_source=finemotorskills&utm_campaign=vmrk-luma-finemotorskills-viam101-learn&utm_content=lp_viam101) (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even the first few lessons will help you get the hang of things quickly.

How to Join

Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis.

We'll select a curated group of ambitious software developers and send official confirmations to accepted participants.

Presented By

Viam (https://www.viam.com/) - The robotics software platform we'll use to configure, control, and deploy models to your robot. Viam makes it easy to get a robot up and running quickly.

## Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hackathon @ NYU

- Record: `luma-crypto-Z0WFxEEVYs4zahG`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-19T14:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/hr-hack-nyc>

### Event Description

Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, and TA practitioners who live this problem every week.

This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), and NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge.

The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel

Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, and candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, and that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it.

You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them.

Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, and a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, and the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet.

The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume.

Questions worth chasing:

- What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one?
- When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness?
- How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people?
- How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it?

Side B - Trust going out: impersonation and candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, and scam job seekers out of money and data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, and easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine.

Questions worth chasing:

- How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company?
- Can impersonating domains be detected and flagged early?
- What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter?

What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel and fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off and easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run.

You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers and builders can go straight at the detection, identity, and verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, and to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made.

### What to Expect

- A full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop
- Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room
- TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works
- A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, and system admins who know these problems cold
- End-of-day demos to judges, investors, and real TA leaders
- The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers

### Prizes

Winners walk away with build-tool and platform credits, expert consulting sessions, and investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders and buyers.

### Judges

- Tiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral and hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships.
- Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator and builder in the HR-tech ecosystem.
- Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside.
- Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel.
- Shiv Jethi (https://www.linkedin.com/in/shiv-jethi/?utm_source=luma) - Engineer at SpaceX.
- Olivia Iarmak (https://www.linkedin.com/in/olivia-iarmak107/) - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality and operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI.
- D. J. Patel (https://www.linkedin.com/in/djpat/?utm_source=luma) - VC | 3x exited founder.
- Prince Rumi (https://www.linkedin.com/in/princerumi/?utm_source=luma) - Excelsior Edge Ventures (https://11-11.madeline.one/?utm_source=luma), Partner | AI Researcher
- Rami Abouemira (https://www.linkedin.com/in/rami-abo/), formerly People Ops at Square and VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR and Founders Foundry.
- Ishaan Das (https://www.linkedin.com/in/ishaanndas/)(TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation and product design for several recruiting firms and recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg.

More judges to be announced - investors and TA buyers joining the panel.

### Who Should Attend

- Engineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML
- Founders and aspiring founders who like shipping fast
- Recent grads, master's students, and NYC college builders
- TA ops and recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers
- HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor

You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, and verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build.

### Credit Sponsors

- Solari (https://www.getsolari.com/) is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, and desktops from one API, and automate at scale.
- Block Convey (https://blockconvey.com) is an AI reliability and observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval and decisions, identify where it fails, and improve it.

### Hosts

- Somya Gupta (https://www.linkedin.com/in/somya-gupta-sg): The face of NYC startup ecosystem.

- Greg Mendez: NYU. Bringing the university's builder and HR-analytics community into the room.
- TechSHRM is NYU Tandon's, award-winning student chapter of the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM). Established in 1987, we bridge data science, technology, and organizational strategy through people analytics - leveraging data to optimize workforce decision-making, recruitment, and employee performance.

## A hackathon to kick off NYC Climate Week 2026

- Record: `luma-crypto-XIU0SEGvG15wUVr`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-19T15:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/n0hzmjij>

### About the event

It's 2026 and we have all seen the simultaneous heating-up of both the AI economy and the average global temperature. Given the rapidly unfolding change, it's easy to feel helpless, uncertain, or concerned when AI usage and tokenmaxxing exist in one sphere and planetary boundaries and climate urgency exist in another. How much does compute usage matter anyway? What is our responsibility of AI in society? And what can we actually control both personally and professionally?

As part of the kickoff to Climate Week 2026, we are going to engage directly with these questions, together. This is a multi-disciplinary hackathon, and you do not need to come in knowing how to code! Your solution can be a poem, a business plan, a research study. And yes, you can build software, but if you plan to build like a super regular normal app as your solution, please make sure to partner with a team members with interesting ideas that can expand your thinking.

### Inspiration tracks for solutions

- Solutionsmaxxing
- Carbon positive AI setups
- Emotions, ethics, and culture

Compute used for this hackathon will be tracked/estimated, and carbon offsets will be purchased.

Participants will have 4 hours to develop something to share. Whether you're into software, hardware, art, communication, policy, finance, business, or just somone who is curious, we hope to see you there.

To attend only the demo portion of the event, please select the "demo only" option when registering, and please plan to attend from 4:30pm to 6:30pm.

Food and beverages will be provided.

### Agenda

- 11:00am gather and meet
- 11:30pm small teams are formed, problem context from industry experts
- 12:00pm hack
- 4:30pm hackers present their demos
- 6:00pm judging and networking

What to bring: your climate-interested and solutions-focused attitude, your laptop or pen+paper, and your unique skillset.

Challenge Statements: the challenge statements will focus entirely on the intersection of AI usage and climate. More details and datasets for these challenge statements will be announced leading up to the event.

Deliverables: the format is intentionally open-ended. More detail on how to format and submit the deliverables will be announced leading up to the event.

Teams: you can create your team of three at the event, or come with a team already formed.

Why this problem? It's one of the most often requested hackathon topics. Will we come out the other side with our beliefs intact? Who knows!

This event is hosted in partnership with Clean Energy Commons. CEC is building a collaborative AI ecosystem for the clean energy industry. Through a cooperative model focused on data sovereignty, CEC brings together data from developers and operators to create AI that understands real-world challenges.

Have an idea for the Challenge Statements, or want to help with this hackathon? Reach out to danbakke1@gmail.com

Projects should be newly created or meaningfully developed during the hackathon. Judging will focus primarily on the progress made during the event.

### Team format

Recommended team size: 3-5 people. Solo participation is also welcome.

You may apply individually or with an existing team. If applying with a team, each member must submit a separate application and receive approval.

Participants who are interested in joining a team will have an opportunity to connect with other participants during an on-site team formation session at the beginning of the hackathon. Team placement is not guaranteed.

### 1. Startup Support & Investment Opportunities

- 2nd Place: $1,000
- 3rd Place: $500

Best Project Built with ElevenLabs - Each team member will receive 3 months of the ElevenLabs Scale plan, valued at $897 per person, with 1.8M credits per month.

### Benefits for All Participants

Every participant will receive $50 in Nebius credits, 1 month of the ElevenLabs Creator plan (a $22 value with 131K credits), and access to the evening networking reception, where they can connect with fellow builders, founders, mentors, and investors.

To be eligible for ElevenLabs benefits, participants must register for Dream AI Hackathon 2026 by 4:00 PM PT on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, and be approved to attend.

## The Agent Harness Hackathon

- Record: `luma-crypto-x4XWFqVISgA8ctG`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

- Original page: <https://luma.com/truefoundry-agent-harness-hackathon-sep19-2026>

### Agent Harness Hackathon

Organized by TrueFoundry and HackerSquad. Sponsored by OpenAI.

AI agents are easy to prototype and much harder to run in production. Once an agent touches real users, tools, data, budgets, and internal systems, the work expands into routing, permissions, tracing, retries, evals, guardrails, cost controls, and deployment.

Join TrueFoundry (https://www.truefoundry.com/) and HackerSquad (https://hackersquad.io) for a full-day hackathon focused on building production-minded agentic applications with TrueForge (https://trueforge.dev), with sponsorship from OpenAI (https://openai.com/).

Take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something you can observe, govern, evaluate, and operate. TrueFoundry's AI Gateway, Agent Gateway, and MCP Gateway will frame the day, with practical work on model routing, controlled tool access, MCP workflows, observability, eval loops, fallback behavior, budget controls, and deployment.

Bring a laptop, a concrete use case, and a willingness to build under realistic production constraints.

### What You Can Build

- An agent workflow with model routing, retries, and fallback behavior
- A tool-using agent with controlled MCP or API access
- An observability layer for traces, tool calls, latency, usage, cost, and failures
- An eval or test harness for agent behavior across repeated runs
- A governance pattern for permissions, approvals, logging, blocking, or escalation
- An agent application that demonstrates how it could run inside a real team or platform environment

### The Challenges We'll Explore

- Coordination: Connecting models, tools, permissions, memory, and context into reliable workflows
- Visibility: Understanding what an agent did, why it did it, and what changed between runs
- Reliability and cost: Managing quotas, budgets, latency, provider failures, retries, and fallbacks
- Runtime controls: Defining what data agents can access, which tools they can call, and when human approval is required
- Deployment: Connecting agents to internal systems while maintaining governance and reliability as usage grows

### Who Should Apply

- Platform, infrastructure, and backend engineers building or operating AI agent systems
- AI and product engineers working with LLMs, tool calling, MCP, evals, or agent workflows
- Technical founders moving agent prototypes toward production
- Security, DevOps, and ML platform practitioners working on governance, observability, and cost control
- Builders with a concrete agent use case and enough technical experience to build during the day

### Format

- Check-in, coffee, and setup
- Welcome from HackerSquad and TrueFoundry
- TrueFoundry Agent Harness introduction
- Challenge brief, build tracks, and judging rubric
- Focused build time with technical support available
- Project submissions and supporting evidence
- Selected demos, judging, awards, and closing remarks
- Networking and follow-up conversations

### Bring

- Your laptop
- An agent use case, workflow, prototype, or infrastructure problem to work on
- Questions about model gateways, MCP tools, observability, evals, cost controls, deployment, or agent governance
- Any teammates you plan to build with

### Event Details

When: Saturday, September 19, 2026 - 9:30 AM-8:00 PM PT

Where: 3120 Scott Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054

Admission: Free, with approval required. Space is limited, and applications will prioritize technical builders working on relevant agent infrastructure and application problems.

Prizes for top demos

1st - $2,000

2nd - $1,000

3rd - $500

Thank you to OpenAI for sponsoring the hackathon and to AI Global Campus (https://aiglobalcampus.com/about) for hosting us.

### About the event

International Day of Peace Concert 2026: Live and Free in Times Square

Subtitle line: 24th Annual. NYC Climate Week Kick-Off.

Short description

Six hours of live music, ceremony and global voices in the middle of Times Square, leading to a World Moment of Silence for Peace. Free, open to all, and streaming worldwide.

### About this event

Once a year, Times Square stops being Times Square.

For 24 years, Good News Corporation has brought artists, faith leaders, UN Peace Ambassadors, elected officials and humanitarian organizations to the busiest intersection in the world for one purpose: a public act of peace, held in the open, free to anyone who walks up.

This year's concert runs from 2 PM to 8 PM on September 19 and opens NYC Climate Week. The afternoon is a Peace Party of calmness and celebration, building toward a World Moment of Silence for Peace. The evening turns inward with OMMM, a slower gathering of musicians, teachers and wisdom keepers centered on breath, sound and shared intention.

On the program:

- A remembrance of 9/11 and the Towers of Light, with Dr. Judy Kuriansky and Rita Cosby
- A tribute to Dolly Parton featuring Dionne Warwick, performing "Peace Like a River"
- Woodstock Forever: Peace, Love & Hope, with Richie Havens
- The HIS LIFE musical
- BlingOne and K-Pop World
- Katya Grineva on piano, Luna Valen, Amanda Abizaid, Georgia Fumanti, Gabrielle Garcia, Heidi Little and the WE The World Tour
- Peace messages from Ringo Starr, Michael Douglas and Dr. Jane Goodall
- Global Peace Poles, civic welcomes and humanitarian awards
- OMMM from 5:30 PM, with the Earth Elders, Antonique Smith, Chris Deckker, Caz Coronel and the Monroe Institute, and more

The UN's call for this day is a ceasefire everywhere and unconditional acts of peace. An estimated 1.6 billion people worldwide know the International Day of Peace. This is how New York answers it.

Admission is free. No ticket required. Register here so we can tell you where to meet and what is happening when.

## Moms. Dinner & Dialogue To Redefine Motherhood

- Record: `luma-crypto-JrCiiIu7jmCwsnU`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
