### About the event

Calling all Moms....of kids, of projects, of pets; books; businesses. Mothers of the friend group, the boardroom, the classroom. We welcome you; we need you; we are you, and we wanna hear your voices. Come. Eat. Let's chat.

If this offering caught your eye, it's for you. We invite you, and all people pondering the complexity of motherhood, to join us for dinner and dialogue. Whether you're a mother, hope to become one, or know definitively that you're not and are very pleased with that decision, this is a space for you.

Our aim is to bring unique thinkers - with hungry bellies - together to dialogue about the complex topic of motherhood. A special multi-course meal will fill your belly while fifteen other self identified moms fill the table. Through round-table discussion, guided breakout conversations, and moments for personal reflection, we invite you to open your heart and expand your mind around a topic you may have thought about often.

Your hosts, Sura Hertzberg and Gwen Pelfini, are licensed therapists who work with relationships and consciousness expansion. We've spoken at length about these questions - with each other, with our patients, with our friends and communities, and, naturally, with our own mothers. Too often our voices get siloed: we see the glossy Instagram stories, but we lack spaces for real dialogue. We're especially interested in spaces where people share not only from their own experience, but in how they relate to the experiences of others. Through reflective dialogue and other group tools, we hope to deepen and enrich how we all communicate and process together.

Food and the belly are their own complex questions for moms. We aim to feed your mind and your belly with equal intention - offering nourishment in every corner of your life, and caring deliberately for your digestive and your nervous system alike.

We'd be honored to have you at the table.

## BitcoinMondays NYC - Featuring A Fireside Chat With Dr. W. Scott Stornetta

### About the event

We've got an epic BitcoinMondays NYC on September 21st at Pubkey, featuring a Fireside Chat Dr. W. Scott Stornetta, the most cited person (at 3 mentions) in Satoshi's white paper! Scott's also widely considered to be the co-inventor of the Blockchain. From 1991, his pioneering series of papers and patents, written with Dr. Stuart Haber, laid the foundation for Bitcoin and other digital currencies.

Today, Dr. W. Scott Stornetta is an active investor, mentor, and the CEO of SureMark Digital (https://www.suremark.digital/). which uses the same techniques that undergird the blockchain to create peer-to-peer unforgeable identities.

SureMark: Making Deepfakes Irrelevant

Artificial intelligence makes it easy to create convincing video, audio, documents, and even real-time conversations. As synthetic media spreads, the internet's core problem shifts from detecting fakes to proving what is real. Rather than defeating deepfakes or even detecting deepfakes, SureMark makes them irrelevant.

SureMark cryptographically binds identity to digital content, creating a universal way to verify identity, online content, and real-time communications. As AI proliferates, every platform, enterprise, and financial system will require this infrastructure.

The United Nations has begun using SureMark credentials for official announcements. A major cybersecurity insurance company will quadruple coverage limits for any company implementing SureMark. SureMark is building channel partnerships across cybersecurity insurance, law firms, and news media verticals.

## Battle of the Personal Brains Hackathon 🧠

- Record: `luma-crypto-sBdX3tSZl05miG7`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-21T23:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/sep-21-cognee-aws>

### Cognee, AWS Strands Agent, Docker Sandbox, Bright Data

$100 in credits for everyone. $1000 in prizes for the winners!

Join us for Battle of the Personal Brains, a 5 hour hands-on AI hackathon where you'll build an intelligent personal agent powered by your own data, live information, and create an agentic workflow to take action, all under one roof at the Bright Data office in SOMA.

Build the personal AI agent you've always wanted.

In today's world, it's possible for an AI agent to know what you know - your emails, your documents, meetings, calendar, tasks, files, and other information that's relevant to you - and then act on it.

For this hackathon, the challenge is simple: Build a brain. Build an agent. Then make it do something.

### Event Details

- When: 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM, Monday September 21, 2026
- Where: Bright Data office, San Francisco, CA

### First, Build your Personal Brain

Your agent is only as useful as the information it can understand. So you'll create an AI-powered brain that can combine knowledge from multiple sources:

- Your laptop and local files
- Google Drive and cloud documents
- Personal email and other data sources
- Public information from across the web
- Meeting notes, receipts, photos, schedules, and more

You'll use Cognee's structured AI memory to create your Personal Brain, and Bright Data to discover and retrieve public web data.

### Then, Build your Agent

Once your agent can access the right knowledge, the real fun begins. Build an agent that can find information, reason across it, and take action.

Your agent could:

1. Manage your calendar - Find availability and schedule an appointment automatically.
2. Take notes and remind you later - Capture information and send a reminder exactly when you need it.
3. Turn meetings into action - Read meeting summaries, identify commitments and action items, and build your personal to-do schedule.
4. Handle your expenses - Process receipts, extract the important information, organize them, and prepare expense reports.
5. Organize and share your photos - Process photos, upload them to Google Photos, organize them, and share them with your WhatsApp group.
6. Build your own personal assistant - Create an agent that understands your information, remembers what's important, and helps you get things done.
7. Connect your digital life - Connect to apps and services you use every day, read through information, create notes, identify what matters, and remind you when action is required.

Or build something completely different.

Your brain. Your agent. Your idea.

### The Agentic Stack

We'll provide technologies you can combine to build your agent:

Cognee - The Brain - Create long-term AI memory and a Personal Brain that your agent can search, understand, and reason over. Get $50 of Cognee Cloud Credits.

Bright Data - The Web - Give your agent access to fresh public information from across the web. Get $50 of Bright Data Credits.

Your Data - The Personal Brain - Bring your own files and information from your laptop, Google Drive, and other sources.

AWS Strands Agents - The Agent Harness - Build and orchestrate the agent that reasons, uses tools, and decides what to do next.

Docker Sandboxes - The Sandbox - Give your agent a secure environment where it can run code and perform tasks.

Together, these technologies give your agent something increasingly important:

Data + Memory + Reasoning + Tools + Actions

### The Battle

This isn't just about building another chatbot. We're looking for agents that can understand information and then accomplish something useful.

At the end of the hackathon, each team will demonstrate what their agents can do. Will it remember better? Find better information? Reason across personal, company, and public data? Can it take useful actions?

But most importantly: Can your brain beat the other brains?

### Who Should Attend?

Developers, AI engineers, agent builders, hackers, founders, students, and anyone interested in building the next generation of personal AI agents. You don't need to arrive with a finished idea. Come with a laptop, some curiosity, and a problem you'd love an AI agent to solve. We'll help you build the rest.

### What to Expect?

- $100 free credits ($50 from Cognee + $50 from Bright Data)
- $1000 in prizes for the top 3 winners! $500, $300, $200
- High-Energy Building Sessions: 5 hours to prototype cutting-edge data and agentic workflows
- Data & AI Challenges: Solve real-world problems that you and others can benefit from
- Expert Mentorship: On-site guidance from developer advocates from Cognee, AWS and Bright Data.
- Swag, Catering & Networking: Fuel up with snacks and food while connecting with fellow builders and founders.
- Prizes & Demos: Win prizes and pitch your build directly to industry leaders.

### What You'll Leave With

By the end of the hackathon, you'll have gone beyond prompts and chatbots. You'll have built an agent with:

- A brain that remembers.
- Knowledge it can retrieve.
- Tools it can use.
- And the ability to take action.

Welcome to the Battle of the Personal Brains.

Build your brain. Build your agent. Enter the battle.

Event Terms & Consent

By registering, you agree to the event terms and conditions. Cognee reserves the right to refuse admission or remove attendees at its discretion to keep things safe and enjoyable for everyone.

Photography and video recording will take place throughout the evening and may be used by Cognee and Bright Data for future marketing, promotional, and community content. By registering, you also consent to receiving the Cognee newsletter and updates about future events at the email address you provide. You can unsubscribe anytime via the link in any email.

Spots are limited. Register now and build the future of Personal Brains.

### About the event

As capital markets, payments and FX infrastructure move onchain the question is: Can the City of London move fast enough to keep its place among the world's leading financial centres?

Global connectivity is reshaping finance faster than ever. With capital markets hubs from NYC to Singapore competing for the same tokenised assets, the choices made in London over the next few years will determine whether we lead the transition or watch it happen from afar.

We're hosting an evening of expert panels addressing the real-world implementation of blockchain and digital asset technology in the UK with representatives from the Digital Asset industry, financial institutions, public sector and regulators.

The evening will conclude with networking drinks and the opportunity to connect with advisers and industry leaders in the UK.

### The Panels

1 - Capital Markets: Opportunities for the City

Can tokenised equities and other onchain products revitalise London's position as a premier capital markets hub?

- Tim Meggs, Co-Founder and CEO, LO:TECH
- Darren Jordan, Chief Commercial Officer, Komainu
- Madush Gupta, Councilor, City of London Corp and Markets Innovation and Strategy Leader, Lloyds Banking Group

2 - The Future of Tokenised Cash in the UK

GBP stablecoins, tokenised deposits, and CBDCs in an evolving regulatory landscape.

- Ryan Hayward, MD of Digital Assets, Barclays
- Sasha Mills, Executive Director of Financial Market Infrastructure, Bank of England
- Gareth Davies MP, Shadow Financial Secretary, House of Commons
- Will Harborne, CEO of Rhino.fi

3 - FX Trading Moves Onchain

How blockchain infrastructure is transforming FX markets, settlement, and liquidity.

- Simone Cortese, Chief Product Officer, Fnality
- Brian Nolan, Co-Founder & CEO, Finteum

Hosted by the UK chapter of the Digital Assets Association (https://digitalassetsassociation.org/), a global non-profit association founded in Singapore in 2023, advancing institutional engagement with blockchain and real-world asset tokenisation, with 150+ members globally. Co-hosted by Komainu (https://komainu.com/).

## Centering Human Dignity in the Age of AI - Side Event on the Margins of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly

- Record: `luma-crypto-nF5sO8DSZQqZAyQ`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-23T13:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed

### About the event

Organizers: Microsoft, Apne Aap International, A.F.I. World Peace Initiative, International Cocoa Diplomacy Eti-Oni Development Group, Generative AI for Good

Co-sponsors: Vital Voices, British Standards Institution, NYU Ethical Tech CoLab, Equality Now, Black Basalt Foundation, Women for Afghanistan, Mediators Beyond Borders International, We are NOT Weapons of War, Cocoa Town and Visions of Peace Initiative, Women Voices Now, Save Ukraine.

Aligned with: the UNGA81 theme, "Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All"; the UN International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026; and SDGs 5, 16, and 17.

### Program

9:00 - 9:30 am | Registration and Networking

ASH Art Exhibit by Black Basalt Foundation. Works on paper created using ash collected from sites destroyed during the July 2025 violent events in Swaida, Syria.

9:30 - 9:45 am | Welcome Remarks

- Yorke E. Rhodes III, Director of Traceability, Microsoft; Adjunct Professor, NYU Center for Global Affairs; Co-founder, Ethical Tech CoLab
- Her Royal Majesty Queen Angelique-Monét of Eti-Oni, Osun State, Nigeria Royal Patron, Eti-Oni Development Group, AFI World Peace Initiative, and International Cocoa Diplomacy

9:45 - 10:30 am | Session 1: From Testimony to Accountability: A UN Framework Protocol on CRSV

Moderator: Tatiana Kotlyarenko, Member of IF20 Advisory Group on Human Trafficking

Despite a robust body of international humanitarian, human rights and criminal law addressing conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), a persistent gap remains between international commitments and their effective implementation at the national level.

This high-level panel will examine the case for a United Nations Framework Protocol on the Implementation of International Obligations relating to Conflict-Related Sexual Violence and Survivor-Centred Responses, a practical framework designed not to create new legal obligations, but to help States translate existing commitments into effective prevention, reporting and documentation, national response frameworks, justice and accountability, comprehensive referral mechanisms, and long-term support for victims and survivors.

Building on existing international standards and good practices, including the Murad Code, the discussion will consider how a Framework Protocol could strengthen survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches, national coordination and international cooperation, while addressing emerging challenges and opportunities related to digital evidence, artificial intelligence and responsible innovation. The panel will bring together experts to identify priority implementation gaps and launch a global consultation process towards the development of the Framework Protocol.

- Fawzia Koofi, President, Women for Afghanistan
- Céline Bardet, Founder and President, We are NOT Weapons of War (WWoW)
- Jay Rosenzweig, CEO, Rosenzweig & Company; Honorary Chair, Raoul Wallenberg Centre for Human Rights; Senior Fellow, Munk School of Global Affairs & Public Policy
- Tsitsi Matekaire, Director, Regions, Equality Now
- Mandy Sanghera, International Human Rights Advocate

10:30 am - 10:45 | Session 2: Fireside Chat | Developing a standard for human dignity

A fireside chat on the development of a standard on human dignity by the British Standards Institute, covering critical areas such as human rights due diligence, modern slavery, safeguarding, violence against women, and diversity, equality, and inclusivity. The discussion will also highlight how standardisation can play a role in preventing crimes linked to these issues, including money laundering, bribery, and fraud.

- Kevin Hyland OBE, Chief Executive Officer, Praevani Global and UK's first Independent Anti-Slavery Commissioner
- Fr. Márcio Toniazzo, Executive Director, Scalabrini International Migration Network

10:45 - 11:00 am | Session 3: Fireside Chat | Hearing Their Voices: Survivor Testimony in the Age of AI

Presentation of a survivor testimony developed through the Hearing Their Voices ethical framework, grounded in the principles of informed consent, transparency, authenticity, safety and non-discrimination, alongside additional testimonies developed with survivors from active conflict zones. The screening will be followed by a short discussion exploring the ethical and practical challenges of collecting, safeguarding and sharing survivor testimony during ongoing conflicts, including how to ensure that survivors retain agency and control over their stories while minimizing risks of retraumatization, stigma and retaliation.

- Yorke E. Rhodes III, Director of Traceability, Microsoft; Adjunct Professor, NYU Center for Global Affairs; Co-founder, Ethical Tech CoLab
- Shiran Mlamdovsky Somech, Founder & CEO, Generative AI for Good

11:00 - 11:45 am | Session 4: AI for Peace: Centering Survivor Voices

Moderator: Dr. Estera Borcsa, psychotherapist and trauma expert, Mediators Beyond Borders International

As conflicts, repression and violence continue to affect communities worldwide, artificial intelligence presents new possibilities for ensuring that the voices and experiences of survivors are heard - while also raising critical questions about safety, dignity, consent, authenticity and the risk of retraumatization. This session will explore how AI and emerging technologies can be used responsibly to amplify survivor voices, preserve testimony, support truth-telling and accountability, and contribute to peacebuilding without exposing survivors to further harm, stigma or retaliation.

Moderated through a trauma-informed lens, the discussion will examine what it means to place survivors, not technology, at the centre of innovation, including the safeguards needed to ensure meaningful consent, survivor agency and control over how testimony is collected, preserved and shared. Bringing together human rights advocates, practitioners and civil society leaders, the panel will consider how survivor-centred AI can help bridge the distance between lived experience and decision-making, ensuring that those most affected by violence and conflict are not simply subjects of international action, but active participants in shaping justice, reconciliation and sustainable peace.

- Manira Alva, Senior Adviser SDG 5, Vital Voices
- Marjan Keypour Greenblatt, Iranian Human Rights Advocate and Analyst, Director of Humanitarian Partnerships, Project Aftab
- Nadia Muradi, program Director, Black Basalt Foundation
- Cate Carbonaro, Executive Director, The Retreat
- Megs Shah, Founder and CEO, Parasol Cooperative

11:45 am - 12:00 pm | Session 5: From Words to Impact: A Goodwill Perspective

- Ruchira Gupta, Apne Aap Women Worldwide; Emmy-winning documentarian, author I Kick and I Fly, Prof, NYU
- Manira Alva, Senior Adviser SDG 5, Vital Voices
- Nika Kovac, Institute 8th of March My Voice, My Choice Democracy Hub

12:00 pm - 1:00 pm | Session 6: Centering Human Dignity in the AI Stack: Technology, Investment and Policy for Human Rights

How do we move responsible AI for human rights from promising innovation to sustainable, scalable infrastructure? This session brings together technology leaders, human rights practitioners, humanitarians and policymakers to examine what it will take to fund, build and scale a responsible AI stack for human rights, peace and security.

The conversation will explore the ecosystem needed to take solutions from prototype to deployment, including responsible AI models, trustworthy data and content provenance, traceability, safeguards, ethical voice and media technologies, and sustainable investment models. The panel will examine the respective roles of technology companies, venture capital, governments, civil society and multilateral institutions in ensuring that innovation reaches the people and communities that need it most.

The discussion will ask a central question: how can we mobilize technology, policy and capital at scale while ensuring that human rights, safety, accountability and human dignity remain embedded in the architecture of AI from the outset?

- Len Khodorkovsky, Senior Advisor to the Chairman, Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue
- Breeze Liu, CEO, Alecto Foundation
- Yorke E. Rhodes III, Director of Traceability, Microsoft; Adjunct Professor, NYU Center for Global Affairs; Co-founder, Ethical Tech CoLab
- Shane Martin, Venture Capitalist, B Ventures Group
- Gabi Leibowitz, Impact, Elevenlabs
- Meagan Fallone, Lead, Schwab Foundation Global AI for Social Innovation Coalition, WEF

1:00- 2:00 pm | Lunch

2:00 - 2:10 pm | Goodwill Message

Cheryl Halpern, Award Winning Filmmaker, Former Director of Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), and Co-Founder of Visions of Peace Initiative

2:10 - 2:30 pm | Session 7: Fireside Chat | The Puppet & The Algorithm: Preserving Human Agency in Next-Gen Storytelling

Fireside Chat: Her Majesty Queen Angelique-Monét, The Queen Consort of Eti-Oni and Tatiana Kotlyarenko, Member of IF20 Advisory Group on Human Trafficking

The entertainment industry has shifted from experimenting with AI to relying on it as an operational foundation. While public friction and union battles dominate headlines, the day-to-day reality of global media uses AI to manage crushing workloads, automate script summaries, and translate content globally in real time. Hosted by global humanitarian and master ventriloquist Queen Angelique Monet, this panel bridges the gap between Silicon Valley innovation and moral responsibility. The discussion frames AI through the metaphor of ventriloquism: an instrument that requires a human soul to truly captivate an audience.

The fireside chat will discuss the immediate future of entertainment, including mobile-first vertical micro-dramas, interactive media featuring persistent AI characters, and AI "world models" that allow indie filmmakers to build massive cinematic environments without Hollywood budgets. Ultimately, the panel outlines the Human Precision Generative Workflow (HPG), a framework ensuring that while technology handles the heavy technical lifting, creative authorship, nuance, and human taste remain firmly protected.

2:30 - 3:15 pm | Session 8: The Cocoa Renaissance Initiative: Empowering Women Cocoa Farmers Through Artificial Intelligence, Cocoa Diplomacy and Sustainable Development

Moderator: Her Majesty Queen Angelique-Monét, The Queen Consort of Eti-Oni

Presented by: AFI World Peace Initiative, International Cocoa Diplomacy, and the Eti-Oni Development Group, in celebration of the UN International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026.

Women perform essential roles across every stage of the cocoa value chain yet receive the smallest share of its economic benefit. This high-level session highlights women cocoa farmers as drivers of sustainable development and showcases how responsible AI, cocoa diplomacy, traditional leadership, and international partnerships can expand productivity, financial inclusion, and climate resilience while preserving indigenous agricultural knowledge. Anchored by the Cocoa Renaissance Initiative, led by His Majesty Oba Dokun Thompson GUREJE IV, The Oloni of Eti-Oni.

Includes a special screening of a 10-minute documentary celebrating women cocoa farmers and the Kingdom of Eti-Oni's 130-year cocoa legacy.

- Dr. Charles Diji Akinola, MD/CEO South West Development Commission, Nigeria
- Mr. Fuad Abubakar, MD, Ghana Cocoa Marketing Company, United Kingdom
- Mrs. Nettie Atkinson, Author and Chocolate Educator
- Ms. Saila Balasubramanian, Chief Operating Officer of Cocoa Town

3:15 - 3:45 pm | Session 9: Ethical Tech CoLab Showcase: Human Dignity, Climate Resilience, and Responsible AI in Practice

- Moderator: Yorke E. Rhodes III, Director of Traceability, Microsoft; Adjunct Professor, NYU Center for Global Affairs; Co-founder, Ethical Tech CoLab and Ruchira Gupta, Apne Aap Women Worldwide; Emmy-winning documentarian, author I Kick and I Fly, Prof, NYU

Presented by: Graduate Researchers of the NYU Ethical Tech CoLab

The NYU Ethical Tech CoLab was founded to explore a central question: How can emerging technologies improve the human condition? Through applied research and prototype development, graduate student researchers work at the intersection of artificial intelligence, human rights, sustainability, migration, diplomacy, labor rights, and public trust.

This showcase highlights practical technology interventions developed by the CoLab that are directly relevant to the themes of human dignity, climate resilience, sustainable development, and ethical AI. Researchers will present a series of rapid demonstrations illustrating how emerging technologies can support communities facing climate disruption, strengthen supply-chain labor accountability, improve crisis response, preserve cultural heritage, and enhance international cooperation.

3:45 - 4:00 pm | Closing and Call to Action

- Ruchira Gupta, Apne Aap Women Worldwide; Emmy-winning documentarian, author I Kick and I Fly, Prof, NYU
- Tatiana Kotlyarenko, Member of IF20 Advisory Group on Human Trafficking

4:00 - 5:00 pm | Royal Cocoa Reception: A Taste of Chocolate from Around the World Celebrating Women Cocoa Farmers

## Superpollutant Action Summit

### About the event

The Superpollutant Action Summit, convened by Beyond Alliance, is a first of its kind gathering for high-level leaders across business, science, government, and civil society to come together for a full day to accelerate action on the pollutants driving the most near-term warming: methane, black carbon, N₂O, and HFCs.

Rapid reductions over the next decade could meaningfully bend the warming curve before mid-century, making this one of the fastest and most immediate levers available for climate progress, with the added benefit of real air quality and health gains along the way.

Momentum on superpollutants has been building across governments, companies, and civil society, from the Global Methane Pledge to a wave of new corporate commitments like the Superpollutant Action Initiative, a $100 million effort from Amazon, Autodesk, Figma, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Salesforce, and Workday to fund high impact mitigation projects, coordinated by Beyond Alliance.

The event will bring together 150+ decision-makers driving climate action in business, finance, policy, and innovation. Through deep dives on corporate Scope 3 action, emerging market mechanisms, voluntary carbon markets, and the policies and financing needed to scale solutions, the day is built for candid dialogue and real commitments.

Across the day, expect candid actionable plenary conversations on where science, policy, and capital meet, thematic breakouts, a look at what it will take to finance faster action at scale, and a showcase of real solutions from the innovators and project developers building them.

## Banking: From Boring to Climate Superpower

- Record: `luma-crypto-KFzHnmUFY8BIh7x`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-23T17:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/g0f8f1k7>

### About the event

We've been programmed to think of banking as a utility: boring by design. Simply a safe place to park our money. A decision with little consequence beyond the financial.

But nothing could be further from the truth.

Our everyday banking decisions generate massive emissions and fuel an invisible hand driving the climate crisis as well as social and environmental injustice around the world. In fact, research from Topo Finance found that, for many of the world's largest companies, the emissions generated by their cash and investments exceeded all their other emissions combined: their operations, their products, even their AI.

We have an opportunity to change that. By leveraging our financial management, we can drive positive impact and help transform the financial system into a visible hand for environmental and social progress around the world.

Join us for an exciting conversation about how corporations, municipalities, organisations and individuals are transforming their banking from one of their largest climate drivers into one of their greatest superpowers.

Panellists include:

- Paul Moinester, Founder and Executive Director, Topo Finance
- Jessica Nelson, Corporate Sustainability Strategy Specialist, Ben & Jerry's
- Craig Hill, Vice President, Client & Treasury Manager, Beneficial State Bank
- Moderated by Amanda Ellis, Co-chair, New Carbon Economy Consortium

### Co-organized with NUS Enterprise and TUM Venture Labs

Time to Accelerate Global Defense Innovation:

Join 120+ of the world's most driven engineers, founders, and operators at the Singapore Defense Tech Hackathon (SDTH) on September 25-27, 2026.

This isn't a typical hackathon. It's a premier global launchpad for defense technology. Work alongside international talent, defense innovators, and industry leaders to tackle real-world security challenges together.

Meet potential co-founders. Build something that actually matters.

### Our Mission

Readying the Little Red Dome -

The future of attritable aerial salvos will overwhelm traditional, sequential air defense systems. Revamp these legacy systems with the next generation of technology: With agentic AI, physics & digital twins at its core, compose robust defense products with commercially available technology. Build a new, comprehensive and investable idea that will secure safer skies. Getting sensors, C2, and shooters right is only half the battle. The other half is manufacturing and sustaining low-cost interceptors locally, without being held hostage by export controls or distant logistics chains. Agentic AI, next-generation perception, and additive manufacturing are three parts of the same answer.

Main Category: 2-day Challenge

2-day challenge tracks will be revealed to all registered participants one week before the event. Apply as a Hacker.

### Focus Areas

- Autonomous Command & Control (C2)
- AI & Agentic Systems
- Sensor-to-Shooter Integration
- Counter-UAS & Drone Swarms
- Maritime Security & Littoral Defense
- Electronic Warfare (EW)
- Resilient Communications
- Space-Based Infrastructure & Defense
- Modular, Integrated Defense Systems
- "Defense Dome" architectures for city-scale protection

By Invitation Only: 3-Month Extended Challenge

A small number of applicants will be personally invited to take on a 3-Month Extended Challenge - an exclusive track for teams ready to work on problems a weekend cannot contain. Harder, more consequential, and deliberately ambitious. 3-months to work on three open questions to build on our mission, or the domain of your choice, at the frontier of defense technology:

### Track A

Can we build interceptors fast, cheap, and smart enough to match modern drone warfare, without skilled pilots or expensive supply chains?

### Track B

Can we design a sensing architecture that holds its picture when hundreds of threats arrive simultaneously?

### Track C

Can we keep meaningful human judgment in the loop when autonomous warfare has already outrun human reaction time?

### Track D

Based on your work and interests, you may also work on deep-tech in the domain of your choice, as long as it is relevant to defense. Do tell us more about your prior experience when you apply as a Hacker.

Selected teams receive mentorship, a per-project budget, and upgraded prizes. Apply as a Hacker. We'll be in touch.

(You may participate in both the 3-month & 2-day challenges!)

### The Prizes

Prizes worth up to $30,000, including a $12,000 top prize.

SDTH is Phase 1 of a 9-month incubation program through the NUS Defence Tech Venture Lab.

The strongest teams get incubated at NUS with milestone-based funding, mentorship, access to defence testbeds and expert and investor networks.

It is a direct pathway from first prototype to funded defense startup, with roots in Singapore, solving challenges that matter globally.

More details will be shared in June.

### About the event

Long-horizon agents still break down over time: they accumulate observations, actions, and stale context until the growing history slows them down, costs more, and makes their own state less reliable.

Fixing that means rethinking the architecture - explicit mutable state instead of ever-growing histories, agents that edit their own working context, and a clear split between what needs to persist and what can be discarded. This hackathon is about building that architecture.

Build systems that help agents preserve what matters and discard what doesn't, staying reliable as tasks stretch from minutes to hours, days, or longer.

### We're backing you with some of the best tools

AWS: The models and cloud infrastructure to help you actually ship

Liquid AI: Efficient general-purpose AI at every scale.

Nimble: Web data your agents can trust

## Build Your AI Co-Founder Hackathon

- Record: `luma-crypto-oesgABTmPAizIxy`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-26T16:00:00.000Z

### About the event

If you have registered on here, please join discord channel as well: https://discord.gg/Ku3GdmbUx7

You bring the idea. Build the AI that makes it happen.

### The Challenge

Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2-4 co-founders, combining humans and AI.

Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder. You decide the rest - including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together.

AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs.

The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team - from idea to execution to a shipped product.

Build the Product challenge using Emergent

Using Emergent, build and ship a functional app or MVP for a real-world problem. Your product should be something real people can use and should demonstrate how your human-AI founding team turns an idea into a working company.

The focus is on execution: build a useful product, validate it with real users, and show what your AI co-founder contributed to the journey from idea to launch.

### Optional Tracks

Build It: Launch the Business

Turn your idea into a launch-ready business. Your AI co-founder helps with research, permits, costs, suppliers, branding, operations, and the launch plan.

Fund It: Raise Capital

Prepare your company to raise funding. Your AI co-founder researches investors, finds the right fit, builds fundraising materials, and helps manage outreach.

Sell It: Get Customers

Get your first customers. Your AI co-founder identifies prospects, researches them, creates personalized outreach, and supports the sales process.

Grow It: Acquire Users

Build a repeatable growth engine. Your AI co-founder helps define your audience, develop positioning, test channels, run experiments, and measure results.

Make It: Build the Product

Turn an idea or problem into a working product. Your AI co-founder helps validate the problem, define the MVP, design the experience, build, test, and iterate.

Run It: Operate the Business

Make your business run better. Your AI co-founder helps improve processes across scheduling, customers, team coordination, reporting, inventory, and automation.

Choose your own

How It Comes Together

The company is up to you. The co-founders are up to you. The roles are up to you. The track defines what you want to accomplish. For example:

Company is AI bookkeeping platform. Co (https://platform.Co)-founders are Human CEO + Human CTO + AI Product + AI Sales

Track is Sell It. Build the product, find potential customers, run outreach, and aim to secure the first paying customers.

Company is AI travel startup. Co (https://startup.Co)-founders are Human Product Lead + AI CEO + AI Growth. Track is Grow It. Build the product, define the target audience, launch growth experiments, and acquire the first users.

Company is Developer productivity tool. Co (https://tool.Co)-founders are Human CTO + AI Product + AI Marketing. Track is Make It. Validate the problem, build the MVP, test it with developers, and ship a working product.

Choose your company. Build your founding team. Pick your mission. Then go build.

We are currently looking for sponsors and partners to support our initiative. Please email events@crewbasecollective or saurabhskhire@gmail.com for details

## Claude for Blockchain: Trading Agents

- Record: `luma-crypto-ujvKacbC5DsvFEC`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-29T08:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/claudeweb3>

### About the event

Pre-TOKEN2049 edition - Claude Singapore Community

In March, OKX did something no major exchange had done: they open-sourced a toolkit that lets an AI agent trade directly on their platform. Spot, futures, options, grid bots - 80+ tools, MIT licensed, running locally on your machine.

Most of the industry still hasn't looked at it.

This session is a straight, practical hour on what exchange-native AI trading actually is, what it can and can't do, and what it means for how you work.

What we'll cover

What OKX actually shipped. The Agent Trade Kit, how it plugs into Claude Code through MCP, and the real scope of what an agent can reach - market data, order execution, position management, automated strategies.

The security model, honestly. Your API keys stay in a local config file. The model never sees them. Signing happens on your machine. Why that design matters, and where the remaining risk actually sits.

How people are using it. Research and market analysis, monitoring, strategy testing in demo mode, and execution. Where each one genuinely helps, and where it falls apart.

The part nobody wants to say out loud. AI makes mistakes, and you own the losses. What guardrails look like in practice - read-only mode, demo profiles, permission-scoped keys - and why you should never skip them.

Where the edge goes. When every desk can run the same agent on the same public data, what's actually left worth having.

Then we build one, live

Last fifteen minutes: a working agent wired to OKX through Claude Code, pulling live market data, running in read-only mode. From nothing to working, on stage. No laptops needed - just watch how little it takes.

And then, Pre-TOKEN Networking

Traders, founders, researchers, and anyone doing crypto work who wants to understand this properly before TOKEN2049 week takes over.

Run of show

4:00 - Doors Open and networking

4:30 - Talk: Trading Agents

5:30 - Live build: an OKX agent in 15 minutes

5:45 - Open networking

6:30 - Close

### Details

Tuesday, 29 September 2026 - 4:30-6:30 PM

Nothing in this session is financial advice. Automated trading carries real risk of loss.

## Collaborative Agent Hackathon @ Stanford

- Record: `luma-crypto-Ks1XgEhMaGtqKer`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-09-29T16:30:00.000Z

- Original page: <https://luma.com/flwrlabs-bamu>

### Build open agents that work together

The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents using Flower.

Agents are changing what is possible, and their greatest potential emerges when they collaborate safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.

Participants will form teams on the day, develop a working prototype and present it at the end of the event. Each team will explore how open-source collaborative agents of varying complexity can work together safely.

You do not need an existing team or a fully developed idea. Bring your laptop, your interests and a willingness to collaborate.

### The hackathon challenge

Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system using Flower in which the safe collaboration of agent teams is central to the solution.

Projects can range across the full collaborative spectrum. Multiple agents might:

- Automate a task
- Form self-improving loops with one another
- Operate across distributed machines and datasets

Flower (https://flower.ai/) is built together with an open-source community spanning more than 7k users world-wide. Flower simplifies building multi-agent systems, supporting distributed coordination, collaborative learning and inference, and privacy-aware deployment.

Projects from all industries and application areas are welcome - including scientific research, healthcare, finance, education, public services, software development and entirely new forms of human-agent collaboration.

### Team formation

Participants register individually.

Teams of two to four people will be formed during the morning, unless formed earlier. The organisers will help participants find teammates with complementary interests and experience.

Already know your team? Please provide your teammates' names when registering.

Bringing an idea is optional.

Eligibility: Everyone is welcome, including builders from startups and companies, as well as students, researchers, and postdocs from all universities.

### Awards

Awards will be presented at the end of the day to recognise outstanding projects and contributions.

Further details about prizes and the selection process will be shared before the event.

### Schedule

9:30-10:00 - Opening, check-in and breakfast

Meet other participants and share your interests and experience.

10:00-10:15 - Welcome

Introduction to the event, the challenge and the day's practical arrangements.

10:15-10:45 - Collaborative agents with Flower

A technical introduction covering collaborative agent architectures, safe coordination, self-improvement loops and the available Flower resources.

10:45-11:00 - Team formation

Meet potential collaborators and form teams of two to four, unless your team was formed earlier.

11:00-12:45 - Build session

Define the project, design the agent interactions and begin implementation.

12:45-1:30 - Lunch

1:30-5:15 - Build session

Develop and test the system, refine the collaboration or self-improvement loop and prepare the demonstration. Mentors will be available throughout.

5:15-5:30 - Demo preparation

5:30-6:45 - Project demonstrations

Teams present their projects, followed by brief questions.

6:45-7:30 - Dinner, awards and closing remarks

Enjoy dinner as we celebrate the winning projects and bring the hackathon to a close.

### About the event

You've got a real business problem. Today you build the fix.

Maybe it's a CRM that's actually just three spreadsheets and a prayer. An inventory system nobody trusts. An HR process that lives in someone's inbox. A client portal you've been meaning to build for a year but never had the dev time for.

Bring that problem. By 3 pm, you'll have a working app that solves it.

This isn't a talk about AI. It's a day of building with Claude and Softr, alongside other people running businesses who are tired of waiting on developers to build their internal tools.

This is for you if:

→ You're running ops on spreadsheets that don't talk to each other

→ Your CRM is a mess, and you know it

→ Inventory, stock, or orders are tracked somewhere nobody fully trusts

→ HR processes still live in email threads and shared docs

→ You've wanted an internal portal or dashboard but never had the time or budget to build one

→ You're the person who'd actually use the thing you build today, not just approve it

What the day looks like:

→ 10:00 Doors, coffee, meet the room

→ 10:30 Welcome and a look at what's already been built

→ 11:00 Build session I

→ 12:30 Lunch (on us)

→ 13:15 Build session II

→ 14:30 Show and tell

→ 15:00 Close

Seats are capped at 30, so everyone gets proper help.

Bring a laptop and a specific problem; that's the only requirement.

Lunch is included.

### About the event

AI Commerce Gallery - ZooWork × AI Valley

### What does the next generation of AI-powered commerce look like?

ZooWork and AI Valley are bringing together builders, founders, engineers, designers, and commerce leaders for AI Commerce Gallery - a curated one-day hackathon and interactive showcase for products pushing commerce forward.

On October 3rd, AI Commerce Gallery takes over The Walt Disney Family Museum in San Francisco for a full day of building, demos, and exploration.

Teams will build throughout the day in the Diane Disney Miller Exhibition Hall before the evening program moves into the Main Museum, with presentations in the Theater and Lower Lobby and private access to the Museum's Main Galleries from 6-8 PM.

Teams will build AI-powered products across:

- E-commerce & storefront experiences
- Merchant operations, inventory, fulfillment & payments
- Restaurants, retail, POS & physical commerce
- AI agents, MCP integrations & workflow automation

But this isn't a traditional hackathon.

Instead of spending the evening watching dozens of back-to-back pitches, every team will turn their project into an exhibit for the AI Commerce Gallery Walk.

After the Gallery Walk, the evening moves into the Main Museum for featured demos, awards, networking, and two hours to explore The Walt Disney Family Museum's Main Galleries.

Attendees, judges, partners, and investors will move through the gallery, interact with live demos, meet the builders, and experience what the future of commerce could actually feel like.

Throughout the day, builders will have access to AI tools, APIs, integrations, technical workshops, mentors, and partner resources to help turn ideas into working products.

The strongest projects will be selected as Featured Exhibits and invited to demo on the main stage before the Gallery Awards.

Awards include

Best in Gallery

October 3rd, 2026

The Walt Disney Family Museum - San Francisco

100-150 curated builders, founders, investors & industry leaders

25-35 teams

### About the event

As digital assets move from the margins into core financial infrastructure, financial crime risk (FCR) teams face a widening set of challenges - from divergent regulatory expectations to the operational realities of scaling compliance across new product lines.

Join our panel during TOKEN2049 Week in Singapore as senior voices from legal, compliance, and industry unpack how financial institutions and digital asset firms are adapting their financial crime programs for this evolving landscape.

The conversation will cover:

- How financial crime operations differ between digital assets and traditional finance, and where those lines are blurring
- The evolving path to securing and managing US licensing applications
- Structuring reliance arrangements with parent companies or broker-dealer partners
- Operating crypto within a multi-product financial institution
- FCR's expanding remit as products diversify - from prediction markets and perpetuals to retail and stablecoin offerings
- Striking the right balance between rigorous onboarding controls and a seamless client experience

## Digital Assets Summit 2026 (DAS2026)

- Record: `luma-crypto-yx5TMJkA5A4WXw1`

### Programmable Finance: The Next Layer of Global Markets and Systems

The Digital Assets Summit 2026 (DAS2026) returns on 6 October 2026, bringing together senior leaders from financial institutions, regulatory authorities, government agencies, law-enforcement organisations, technology companies and the wider digital-assets ecosystem.

Following the strong success of DAS2025, this year's summit will feature an expanded programme of keynote addresses, expert panels and substantive industry discussions focused on the next phase of institutional digital-asset adoption.

As digital assets move beyond experimentation, the conversation is increasingly shifting towards how blockchain-based infrastructure, tokenised assets and programmable financial systems can operate at scale within global markets.

DAS2026 will examine the opportunities, infrastructure, governance and regulatory considerations shaping this transition.

### What to Expect

The programme will explore key areas including:

- Tokenisation of financial and real-world assets
- Programmable finance and blockchain-based market infrastructure
- Stablecoins, deposit tokens and new settlement rails
- Institutional adoption, custody and wealth management
- The convergence of digital assets and traditional financial markets
- Artificial intelligence and its role in the digital-assets ecosystem
- Regulation, compliance, enforcement and financial-crime prevention
- The evolving roles of banks, intermediaries and market-infrastructure providers

Attendees can expect practical perspectives, candid discussions and deep insights from leaders directly involved in developing, regulating and implementing digital-asset solutions.

### Who Should Attend

DAS2026 is designed for industry professionals, including:

- Financial institutions and banks
- Regulators and government agencies
- Digital-asset and blockchain companies
- Asset managers, investors and family offices
- Custodians, exchanges and infrastructure providers
- Legal, compliance and risk professionals
- Technology and cybersecurity companies
- Professional-services firms
- Policymakers, academics and industry associations

### Afterparty

The summit will be followed by the official DAS2026 Afterparty from 5:30 PM till late, providing attendees with an extended opportunity to connect with speakers, sponsors, partners and fellow industry professionals in a more informal setting.

### Tickets

Early Bird Ticket: S$68

Available until 31 Aug 2026

Standard Ticket: S$88

Available from 1 Sep to 6 Oct 2026

### Complimentary Access for DAA Members

DAA individual members and eligible representatives from DAA corporate member organisations are entitled to complimentary tickets, subject to their respective membership allocations.

Employees of corporate member organisations should contact their organisation's designated DAA representative to obtain the appropriate registration access.

Interested in joining the Digital Assets Association and accessing DAS2026 as part of your membership?

Apply here:

https://digitalassetsassociation.org/membership/

### Event Details

Date: Tuesday, 6 October 2026

Venue: SGX Auditorium

Time: 9:00AM to 9:30PM

Keynote speakers, panelists, sponsors, official partners and the full programme will be announced progressively.

## Merkle Science Meet Singapore: Shaping the Future of Digital Asset Compliance

### About the event

Join Merkle Science for an exclusive Merkle Science Meet in Singapore during Token2049, bringing together senior leaders across digital assets, payments, compliance, regulation, and financial services.

- Sumsub - The first AI-powered trust infrastructure for compliance operations at scale. It connects identity and business verification, fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, and risk workflows, helping teams reduce manual work and enter new markets (https://markets.Global).
- Drew & Napier - Leading Singapore law firm with a dedicated Blockchain & Digital Assets practice advising companies on regulation, licensing, compliance, and digital asset activities.
- Movantis - Global financial infrastructure platform connecting payments, remittances, FX, wallets, and stablecoin settlement across traditional and digital rails.
- Utexo - Payment and settlement infrastructure enabling instant USDT payments and settlement on Bitcoin through APIs and Lightning Network infrastructure.
- Aleo - Privacy-focused Layer-1 blockchain enabling developers to build private and programmable applications using zero-knowledge technology.

### Merkle Science Meet Singapore - Agenda

1:30 PM - 1:50 PM

Arrival & Networking

Light refreshments and informal networking.

1:50 PM - 2:00 PM

Welcome Remarks

Opening remarks from Mriganka Pattnaik, CEO & Co-Founder, Merkle Science, welcoming attendees to the Merkle Science Meet Singapore.

2:00 PM - 2:40 PM

### MAS, MiCA & the Race to Set the Global Standard

Singapore and the EU are pursuing distinct but closely watched approaches to digital asset regulation, with both influencing how jurisdictions across APAC develop their own frameworks.

This panel will compare the MAS licensing regime with MiCA, explore how trading venues and exchanges are structuring their operations across both markets, and examine whether a global standard for crypto regulation is emerging - or whether regulatory fragmentation will remain the defining challenge.

### Speakers

- Wee Siang Lee - Executive Director, Head of APAC Compliance, Paxos
- Markus Franke - Head of Stablecoin, Celo
- Delphine Forma
- Grace Chong - Drew & Napier
- Maggie Qiu - Head of APAC, Bitpanda Enterprise

Moderator: Alvin Wang - CEO, Rheo

2:40 PM - 2:55 PM

Merkle Science Technology Demo

A live demonstration showcasing how blockchain intelligence and analytics can support compliance, risk management and investigations.

2:55 PM - 3:35 PM

- Kelcent Tan - Legal & Regulatory Lead, Reap
- Sophia Roman - Director of Partnerships, Aleo
- Patrick Ngan - CEO, Alchemy Pay
- Zack Yang - Co-Founder, FOMO Pay
- Pei Ling - President, MetaComp
- Tristan Wallaert - CEO, Request Network

Moderator: Donato Pio Gianera - Head of BD APAC

3:35 PM - 3:55 PM

Networking Break

3:55 PM - 4:35 PM

- Ilya Brovin - CGO, Sumsub
- Sheena Lim - CEO, 1exchange
- Jenna Peterson - COO, Midnight Foundation
- Arthur Breitman - Co-Founder, Tezos
- Heslin Kim - Co-Founder & CBO, Zenith
- Yan Ma - Executive Director, Spartan Group

Moderator: Mark Tang - VP, Client Solutions, Hydra X

4:35 PM - 4:50 PM

Merkle Science Technology Demo

A second opportunity to explore Merkle Science's blockchain intelligence and compliance technology through a live demonstration.

4:50 PM - 5:30 PM

- Arnaud Wenger - General Counsel, Sakura Linkage Int
- Jason Chan - Head of Government Relations APAC, Sumsub
- Nick Woolliscroft - Trident
- Mac Thiele - Head of Investigations & Law Enforcement Relations, KAST
- Remi Gai - CEO, Inco
- Summer Yu - Group CCO, Alpha Ladder Group

Moderator: David Suzuki - Founder & CEO, Kikutora Special Risks

### Stablecoins & Cross-Border Payments

Stablecoins are rapidly reshaping cross-border payments and financial infrastructure across APAC.

This panel will examine the regulatory and compliance considerations surrounding stablecoin adoption and digital payment infrastructure, while exploring how financial institutions, payment providers and digital asset companies are navigating an increasingly interconnected market.

### Real-World Asset Tokenization: Compliance at the Intersection of TradFi & Blockchain

Tokenized funds, bonds, real estate and private credit are moving from pilot programmes toward live issuance across Singapore, Hong Kong and Europe.

This panel will explore the compliance infrastructure required to support RWA tokenization at scale - from KYC and investor eligibility controls to secondary-market monitoring and cross-border regulatory coordination.

Speakers will share insights from live deployments and discuss the remaining challenges facing institutions as traditional financial assets move on-chain.

### AML, Sanctions & Crypto Crime in APAC

Southeast Asia has become a focal region for large-scale crypto fraud and financial crime, including pig-butchering scam networks, money mule operations and sanctions-exposed flows.

This panel brings together investigators, compliance professionals and industry experts to examine how illicit networks are evolving, how blockchain analytics can be used to trace and disrupt financial crime, and how cooperation between law enforcement and the private sector can strengthen the regional response.

### 5:30 PM onwards

Networking Reception

Continue the conversation during an exclusive networking reception, bringing together a select group of C-level executives and senior decision-makers from across the digital asset, financial services, compliance and technology ecosystems.

## TOKEN2049 Singapore. Quantum Security for Digital Assets with Industry Leaders

- Record: `luma-crypto-yVvzhRKJfiM98cK`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)
- Starts: 2026-10-07T10:00:00.000Z
- Description: Source-backed
- Original page: <https://luma.com/t7pr9d8o>

### About the event

Quantum Security for Digital Assets

This private technical event brings together industry leaders, protocol engineers, cryptography researchers, digital asset specialists and institutional stakeholders to examine the emerging security requirements of digital assets in a post quantum environment.

The discussion will focus on the cryptographic foundations required to protect digital asset infrastructure as quantum computing develops, including digital signatures, transaction authentication, identity, key management, consensus security and the protection of blockchain execution environments.

Panels with industry leaders will be followed by relaxed networking with senior peers over food and drinks.

Particular attention will be given to the transition from conventional elliptic curve cryptography toward post quantum cryptographic systems and the practical considerations involved in implementing these mechanisms at protocol level.

Topics will include

- Post quantum digital signatures and transaction authentication
- Quantum resistant identity and account structures
- Key generation, address derivation and key lifecycle management
- Post quantum consensus and validator communication
- Cryptographic verification within distributed systems
- Quantum resistant smart contract infrastructure
- Migration considerations for existing digital asset systems
- Security implications for institutional digital asset custody and infrastructure.
- The discussion will also examine how post quantum cryptography can be integrated throughout a blockchain protocol rather than being implemented as an isolated security layer.

Quantova will present its approach to post quantum blockchain architecture, including the Quantova Virtual Machine and its implementation of PQR cryptographic primitives across transaction signing, account creation, consensus and execution.

Attendees will have the opportunity to examine the practical relationship between cryptographic primitives, protocol architecture and application execution, with discussion focused on implementation rather than commercial promotion.

### About organizers

- Quantova (https://Quantova.org) runs a post-quantum Layer 1 network built from first principles to issue, move, settle and protect digital value: digital identity, stablecoins, tokenised real-world assets, payments and institutional settlement, without inheriting a future migration burden.
- Quantova launched QDock.io (https://QDock.io), the development environment supporting post quantum application development, together with the underlying cryptographic libraries, compilation tooling and deployment infrastructure used within the Quantova environment.

Further technical information is available at Quantova.org (https://Quantova.org)

HackenProof is a bug bounty and crowdsourced security platform connecting companies with a global network of white-hat security researchers. The platform supports more than 400 programs, with over $26 million paid in bounties and a community of more than 85,000 ethical hackers.

Anna Tutova has been active in the digital asset industry for many years, working at the intersection of cryptocurrency regulation, institutional finance and quantum security. She has contributed to international regulatory and industry discussions and spoken at events across multiple regions, including on the evolving relationship between digital assets, regulation and post-quantum security.

### About the event

As technology rapidly reshapes industries, job roles, and required skill sets, professionals are increasingly being asked to adapt before the path forward is fully clear. Whether navigating a career transition, responding to AI-driven disruption, repositioning yourself in a competitive job market, or hiring talent for emerging roles, success depends on more than technical expertise - it requires the ability to tell a compelling professional story.

This highly interactive session uses Interactive Business Theater, featuring professional actors portraying realistic workplace and career conversations, to explore how individuals can define and communicate their unique value in a changing world of work. Through facilitated discussion, audience participation, and practical frameworks, participants will learn how to build a professional narrative that aligns their experiences, strengths, and aspirations with evolving employer needs.

Learning Objectives:

- Identify and articulate your unique value proposition in a rapidly evolving labor market
- Translate past experiences and transferable skills into a compelling professional narrative
- Position yourself competitively amid AI, automation, and shifting workforce demands
- Navigate career development conversations with greater confidence, clarity, and adaptability

Facilitator: Rahul Kay, MBA, MPH

Rahul Kay helps organizations develop leaders who can navigate uncertainty, drive performance, and build stronger workplace cultures. As the Director of Client Success, his work focuses on leadership development, organizational effectiveness, and experiential learning. Prior to Ibis, Rahul was the CEO of an employee mental health organization, worked in organizational strategy at McKinsey, and supported change initiatives through the United Nations. He holds an MBA from the MIT Sloan School of Management, and MPH from Tufts Medical, and studied clinical psychology at Cornell.

## Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon

### About the event

The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16-18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area's deep-tech ecosystem.

Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges, with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event.

### Challenge Tracks

1. OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis
2. Piping Layout Optimization
3. Software-Defined Vessel

### Build with Real Hardware

Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.

These tools are intended for hands-on technical development. Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.

Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.

Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event.

### More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon

The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.

- Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.
- Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.
- Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.
- Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri's network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.
- Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem.

### Partners & Ecosystem

The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri (https://www.fincantieri.com/en), Mind The Bridge (https://mindthebridge.com/)and Silicon Mountain (https://www.linkedin.com/company/silicon-mtn/posts/?feedView=all).

Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.

Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judging.

### What to Expect

- 48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping
- Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri
- Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources
- Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event
- Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers
- A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team
- Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon, and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design or prototyping.

Come with a team or find one at the event.

To help us maintain an accurate headcount, a $20 refundable deposit is required to reserve your spot. The deposit will be fully refunded when you attend the event.

Spots are limited - register early to secure your place.

## ExecuTorch Hackathon

- Record: `luma-crypto-uY7AwaQhqCO2Ejy`
- Source: [luma-crypto-events.json](sources/luma-crypto-events.json)

### About the event

NOTE: By registering for the Luma, you are submitting an application to participate. We will reach out on a rolling basis to let you know whether you've been accepted. There are a limited number of devices, we can support up to 200 participants.

This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.

Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder's Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026 (https://opensourceaiweek.com/).

Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm (https://www.qualcomm.com/developer), Meta (https://www.meta.com/), GitHub (https://github.com/), the PyTorch Foundation (https://pytorch.org/foundation/), and Open Intelligence Foundation (https://openintelligence.foundation/), this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch (https://executorch.ai/) - an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.

Participants will work in teams of 3-5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.

Compute Track

Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.

Mobile + XR Track

Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.

IoT Track

Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino® VENTUNO™ Q boards, combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences. Choose from an assortment of modulinos and accessories to complete your project (available on a first come, first served basis).

To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3-5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.

### Prizes

The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.

Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.

Questions? Join our Discord!

Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.

Join here: https://discord.gg/A635v4hMSg

Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

### About Open Intelligence Foundation

The Open Intelligence Foundation (https://openintelligence.foundation/) is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week (https://opensourceaiweek.com/), a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

About Founders, Inc.

Founders, Inc. (https://f.inc/) backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

Snapdragon and Qualcomm branded products are products of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and/or its subsidiaries. Arduino and VENTUNO are trademarks or registered trademarks of Arduino S.r.l.

### About the event

Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

### About the event

The Hong Kong Digital Asset Summit is an institutional event focused on how digital asset infrastructure interfaces with institutional markets.

Held at the Grand Hyatt alongside Hong Kong FinTech Week, the Summit brings together global blockchain infrastructure providers and institutional market participants for structured dialogue on deployment within Hong Kong's regulatory framework.

### PARTNER

Standard event sponsorship delivers a logo, a booth, and a list of badge scans. The Hong Kong Digital Asset Summit is structured differently.

Partnership structures range from targeted business development packages to full event association under your brand. If your organization needs to be present where the APAC digital asset market is being shaped in 2026, tell us your objectives.

[Get in touch (https://www.cosmoverse.org/sponsors-partners)]

### THE VENUE

The Hong Kong Digital Asset Summit takes place at the Grand Hyatt Hong Kong, situated directly alongside the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre on Victoria Harbour.

The Summit runs alongside Hong Kong FinTech Week, making the Grand Hyatt the institutional centre of the most concentrated week of digital finance activity in Asia Pacific.

### Business Day | 4 November (Invite Only)

A closed-door day reserved for confirmed speakers and partners, with private, focused engagement among senior institutional leaders and capital allocators. Participation is by invitation only.

The decision-makers driving digital asset adoption across Asia Pacific will be in the room. Secure your place.

### About the event

Malatya'da buluşuyoruz.

Yazılım, blockchain ve yeni teknolojilerle ilgilenen öğrencileri, geliştiricileri, tasarımcıları ve bir şeyler üretmek isteyen herkesi aynı masada buluşturuyoruz.

Bu, Malatya'daki ilk buluşmamız. Amacımız önce tanışmak, şehirde kimlerin nelerle ilgilendiğini görmek ve birlikte neler çıkarabileceğimize bakmak.

Daha önce Solana, Superteam Türkiye veya blockchain tarafında hiçbir şey yapmadıysan sorun değil. Bu etkinlik zaten biraz da bunun için var.

Kahvelerimizi alacağız, Solana ekosistemini konuşacağız, Superteam Türkiye'nin sunduğu fırsatlara bakacağız ve yaklaşan Colosseum hackathon'una nasıl dahil olabileceğimizi konuşacağız.

Kimler gelebilir?

Yazılımla ilgilenenler

Tasarım yapanlar

Ürün veya girişim fikri olanlar

Kendi projesini geliştirenler

Sadece merak edip tanışmak isteyenler

Bir fikrin ya da ekibin hazır olmak zorunda değil.

Neler konuşacağız?

Solana nedir, ekosistemde neler yapılıyor?

Superteam Türkiye nedir ve hangi fırsatları sunuyor?

Colosseum hackathon'una nasıl dahil olunur?

Ekip nasıl kurulur, bir fikir nasıl projeye dönüşür?

Malatya'dan daha fazla builder ve proje çıkarmak için birlikte neler yapabiliriz?

Ekosistemden sürpriz konuklarımız da olacak.

Kahveler bizden.

Gel, tanışalım ve Malatya'dan neler çıkabileceğine birlikte bakalım.

What is Tech Weekend? A 48-hour fundraising sprint by Founders Village where pre-seed to Series A founders meet dozens of investors in back-to-back meetings.

https://techweekend.org/

Stay Connected

Follow us on socials:

Website: Founders Village (https://beacons.ai/founders_village)

Founders Village Bio (https://beacons.ai/founders_village)

If you have any questions, feel free to email us at events@foundersvillage.co

### Who should attend?

Pre-seed to Series B Tech Startups.

Looking at the investors joining us in September, here's where their attention seems to be for this cohort

▪ Physical AI - robotics, sensors, industrial automation, and the machines reshaping manufacturing, construction, and mobility.
▪ Semiconductors and AI chips - the silicon underneath all of it.
▪ Deep tech, defense, space tech and dual-use, alongside cybersecurity and enterprise infrastructure.
▪ Fintech and financial services - banking technology, financial infrastructure, and the security that protects it.
▪ Health tech and biotech - health and wellness, digital health care solutions, pharma production, oncology, and medical devices.
▪ Climate and energy - adaptation and resilience, clean energy, electrification, batteries, and transportation.
▪ AI, across the whole stack - infrastructure, enterprise, application layer, AI-ready data, and the work of making it safe and interpretable.
▪ And a good number of the investors are sector agnostic, backing exceptional founders building in any industry.

If you're building in any of these areas and looking for capital to scale, consider applying for Tech Weekend Cohort September 2026

Across two days, Founders connect with investors through:

▪ VC Office Hours: 20-30-minute one-on-one meetings with top investors who are investing in your space. At least 8 meetings are assigned to each founder with a cohort pass.
▪ Pitch Competition: Present to a panel of active VCs. Get real-time feedback and offers to chat more offline.
▪ VC Panels & Fireside Chats: Gain insights from investors who've deployed millions. Hear what they're looking for and how to stand out.
▪ Networking Mixer: All-day networking mixers with founders, investors and engineers gathered from across the United States and abroad.

Full event + how VC Office Hours work: https://techweekend.org/office-hours
